item.title: The Outlook - Week 10 (SEA-LV, LAR-ARI, SF-DAL, PIT-CIN, LAC-BAL)
item.description: Hey, folks! We’re back with our third and final block of games for the Week 10 NFL slate, and we’re covering all three late games, Sunday Night Football and Monday Night Football! We’ve compiled the game groupings here to make it easier to find the games you want: Block 1: WAS-NYG, NE-DET, KC-ATL, HOU-CLE, MIA-IND Block 2: JAC-TEN, MIN-GB, CAR-NO, BUF-NYJ Block 3: SEA-LV, LAR-ARI, SF-DAL, PIT-CIN, LAC-BAL “The Outlook” will give you the details, stats, analysis, recommendations and everything else you need to make informed fantasy football decisions. Every fantasy-relevant player on each team will be profiled in this article. We want everyone reading this to bring home championships in their fantasy leagues! I’m incredibly excited to bring this article to all of you this season, and I hope you enjoy the ride. If you have any questions, feel free to find me on Bluesky (@ktompkinsii.bsky.social) or tag me in a post with any lineup questions. I’ll do my best to answer them for you. Let’s get into it! All game and implied point totals listed were compiled via DraftKings Sportsbook on Thursday for SEA-LV, LAR-ARI, SF-DAL, PIT-CIN and LAC-BAL. Teams on bye in Week 9: Chicago Bears, Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Seattle Seahawks at Las Vegas Raiders Favorite: Seahawks –6.5 Game Total: 40.5 Implied Point Total: Seahawks 23.5, Raiders 17 Seahawks Fantasy Notes Must-Start Players: WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba Seahawks RBs In Week 8, both Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returned to action against the Chicago Bears in a gross, ugly backfield split that didn’t benefit either back. In Week 9 against a softer opponent in the Cardinals, the Seahawks were able to get the running game going a little bit in neutral and positive game scripts. Both players were heavily involved, but Charbonnet saw more work than Price. Charbonnet (17) out-touched Price (13), and George Holani was essentially phased out of regular work with just two snaps. Charbonnet was the lead back on the game’s first two drives, after which Price and Charbonnet alternated drives for the rest of the game. Price actually led the Seahawks with 54 receiving yards in a very muted game started by Drew Lock . In this configuration, Charbonnet is ahead of Price for now, and in most situations, Charbonnet should get the edge in receiving work. Think of it as the early Kyren Williams/Blake Corum split, but with Corum getting a bit more of the receiving work while Williams plays the majority of the snaps. Charbonnet certainly isn’t Williams, but if Seattle can find some offensive rhythm, both backs can achieve fantasy viability. Fantasy Advice: With the Raiders giving up the second-most fantasy points per game to backfields, this is a great spot for the Seahawks backs. I’d be happy to fire up Charbonnet as a low-end RB2 and Price as a low-end flex play who should get enough work to matter here. item.content:encoded: Hey, folks! We’re back with our third and final block of games for the Week 10 NFL slate, and we’re covering all three late games, Sunday Night Football and Monday Night Football! We’ve compiled the game groupings here to make it easier to find the games you want: Block 1: WAS-NYG, NE-DET, KC-ATL, HOU-CLE, MIA-IND Block 2: JAC-TEN, MIN-GB, CAR-NO, BUF-NYJ Block 3: SEA-LV, LAR-ARI, SF-DAL, PIT-CIN, LAC-BAL “The Outlook” will give you the details, stats, analysis, recommendations and everything else you need to make informed fantasy football decisions. Every fantasy-relevant player on each team will be profiled in this article. We want everyone reading this to bring home championships in their fantasy leagues! I’m incredibly excited to bring this article to all of you this season, and I hope you enjoy the ride. If you have any questions, feel free to find me on Bluesky (@ktompkinsii.bsky.social) or tag me in a post with any lineup questions. I’ll do my best to answer them for you. Let’s get into it! All game and implied point totals listed were compiled via DraftKings Sportsbook on Thursday for SEA-LV, LAR-ARI, SF-DAL, PIT-CIN and LAC-BAL. Teams on bye in Week 9: Chicago Bears, Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Seattle Seahawks at Las Vegas Raiders Favorite: Seahawks –6.5 Game Total: 40.5 Implied Point Total: Seahawks 23.5, Raiders 17 Seahawks Fantasy Notes Must-Start Players: WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba Seahawks RBs In Week 8, both Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returned to action against the Chicago Bears in a gross, ugly backfield split that didn’t benefit either back. In Week 9 against a softer opponent in the Cardinals, the Seahawks were able to get the running game going a little bit in neutral and positive game scripts. Both players were heavily involved, but Charbonnet saw more work than Price. Charbonnet (17) out-touched Price (13), and George Holani was essentially phased out of regular work with just two snaps. Charbonnet was the lead back on the game’s first two drives, after which Price and Charbonnet alternated drives for the rest of the game. Price actually led the Seahawks with 54 receiving yards in a very muted game started by Drew Lock . In this configuration, Charbonnet is ahead of Price for now, and in most situations, Charbonnet should get the edge in receiving work. Think of it as the early Kyren Williams/Blake Corum split, but with Corum getting a bit more of the receiving work while Williams plays the majority of the snaps. Charbonnet certainly isn’t Williams, but if Seattle can find some offensive rhythm, both backs can achieve fantasy viability. Fantasy Advice: With the Raiders giving up the second-most fantasy points per game to backfields, this is a great spot for the Seahawks backs. I’d be happy to fire up Charbonnet as a low-end RB2 and Price as a low-end flex play who should get enough work to matter here. Raiders Fantasy Notes Must-Start Players: TE Brock Bowers QB Fernando Mendoza With Kirk Cousins now back in Pizza Ranch country , Mendoza will make his first NFL start after watching Cousins for nine games and getting some garbage-time throws in Week 5’s blowout loss in New England. Mendoza will immediately be thrown into the fire at home against the Seahawks before having to travel to Denver to play the Broncos. More than likely, offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko and head coach and playcaller Klint Kubiak will do their best not to put too much on Mendoza’s plate early on. That means conservative playcalling and getting the ball out quickly. It may also mean more running plays, so we’ll see how the Raiders navigate these waters over the next few weeks. Fantasy Advice: Mendoza is worth picking up as a speculative stash. Trusting him as a fantasy starter against Seattle? I doubt anybody is that desperate, unless you are exactly that: desperate. Raiders RBs The split among these Vegas running backs persists, and Mike Washington Jr. took a bit of a backseat to Ashton Jeanty in terms of touches and overall playing time. Jeanty handled an overwhelming 63% of the snaps and 73% of the routes, earning seven targets and catching five passes for -5 yards. I’m sure the anti-PPR bros were up in arms about Jeanty earning seven points on that receiving work and his 25 rushing yards. Meanwhile, Washington’s -0.5 yards per carry likely isn’t impressing anybody. Jeanty has a bit of R.J. Harvey in him right now with his role, and Washington is somebody you don’t need to be plugging into your fantasy lineups. Luckily, Jeanty’s receiving floor could pay some dividends for a young quarterback making his first NFL start. Fantasy Advice: I’d be fine with Jeanty as a flex against the Seahawks in Week 10, but his fantasy stock has really fallen over the last month with Kubiak’s meddling. To be fair, Jeanty hasn’t exactly helped himself here, despite reportedly being banged up. Los Angeles Rams at Arizona Cardinals Favorite: Rams –9.5 Game Total: 39.5 Implied Point Total: Rams 24.5, Cardinals 15 Rams Fantasy Notes Must-Start Players: None QB Matthew Stafford It’s been the running game that has carried Stafford’s offense over the past month. Stafford’s best fantasy finish was QB11 against the Raiders in Week 7. Since then, he’s finished as QB22 against the Chargers and QB20 against the Commanders. He hasn’t had Davante Adams in any of those three games. Now, at least for the foreseeable future, he won’t have Puka Nacua either. You could still make the case for starting Stafford with Nacua in the lineup. Without him, however, it’s a collection of young, inexperienced players, his running backs and a glut of tight ends. That doesn’t make for a very enticing fantasy quarterback, especially when the Rams’ running backs have been driving the offense and they have a below-average matchup against fantasy running backs on tap. I’d be looking elsewhere, despite the Cardinals being one of the best matchups for any quarterback. Fantasy Advice: Stafford is a solid QB2 option who should be able to provide a usable floor, but a ceiling game is almost impossible to expect given the injuries to both Adams and Nacua. Rams RBs This Rams offense will have to rely almost entirely on Kyren Williams and Blake Corum for now, with Adams and Nacua out of the wide receiver lineup. Luckily, Corum has been on a massive heater with five consecutive top-20 fantasy finishes and at least 58 yards and a touchdown in each of those games. Meanwhile, Williams should be able to pick up some of the target-earning slack without Nacua while continuing to provide solid production on the ground. Williams had his worst fantasy performance of the season, finishing as RB25 last week with three receptions and 61 yards from scrimmage against the Commanders. However, if there’s a time for anybody to pick up the pieces of the offense after these two major injuries, it’s now for both Williams and Corum. Fantasy Advice: Both Williams and Corum are viable fantasy RB2s against the Cardinals, with Williams getting a slight edge in PPR formats and the two being nearly even in value in half-PPR. Cardinals Fantasy Notes Must-Start Players: TE Trey McBride RB Tyler Allgeier It feels like Allgeier’s 36.1 fantasy-point outburst against the Cowboys was quite the outlier, as he went right back to averaging 2.7 yards per carry against the Seahawks. To be fair, that was expected. The outburst came against the Cowboys, and he returned to being a plodder against the Seahawks in Seattle. Even more factors are working against him now. Allgeier faces another tough defense at home in Week 10 against the Rams, and Bam Knight may return to work in tandem with him. With Gardner Minshew injured and placed on IR, rookie Carson Beck will start at quarterback this weekend. That combination of factors really pushes Allgeier down the rankings and makes him a volume-based back who may not even get enough opportunities if Knight returns and takes some carries away fro

item.title: Australian cricket's sandpapergate is back - and it cuts deep in a 'nation of good sports'
item.description: Pat Cummins spent over an hour fielding questions over sandpapergate on Friday [Getty Images] As Australian cricket captain Pat Cummins spent more than an hour being grilled by reporters over one of sport's biggest cheating scandals, the tension in the hall was occasionally pierced by muffled cheers. Outside, a crucial match in the top tier of domestic cricket was getting under way. Cummins was clear he'd rather we all be talking about that. But inside the nets at Cricket Central in Sydney, he faced more than a dozen TV cameras and a gaggle of journalists several times as large. His goal: to put rumours of his involvement in "sandpapergate" to rest. "I don't want to talk about this again after today," he said. "Even if it takes all day... I'll stay here until we have no more questions." A book by his friend and former teammate Usman Khawaja has renewed scrutiny on a 2018 plot to tamper with the ball using sandpaper in Australia's third Test match against South Africa in Cape Town. Three players admitted they were involved at the time and were handed lengthy bans, but in a memoir released last week, Khawaja said the entire Australian team knew about the sandpaper scheme. His claims have plunged the Australian cricket world into chaos, thrown speculation over key figures from that Test - including star bowler Cummins who has since risen to hold what many joke is Australia's most important job - and reopened wounds for fans. Josh, 28, told the BBC he thought everyone had moved on: "It's just a bit crazy that it's all blown up again... I think it is a bit ridiculous, after eight years." "I'm a bit bored of it," another spectator at the New South Wales vs South Australia Sheffield Shield match said. Josh says he was surprised the scandal is back in the news [BBC] Among fans, there's frustration that Khawaja has chosen to come forward now, almost a decade on and at the start of an exciting summer, and year, of cricket. Though there's an argument there'd never be a good time for Khawaja, who retired from international cricket in January, to make these allegations. There's worry about the impact on the men's team's performance this summer, after a lacklustre showing in South Africa last month - its first Test matches there since the 2018 incident. There's a sense of injustice that Australia can't escape the scandal, given - according to many players themselves - how common boundary-bending on ball tampering apparently was in that era. "It's a bit of a stitch up," 21-year-old James said. "Every country has done it... if it wasn't us, it was probably going to be someone else." Khawaja has said he owed it to the three players punished to tell his side of the story [Getty Images] Khawaja's memoir is also causing rancour among current and former players and coaches. item.content:encoded: Pat Cummins spent over an hour fielding questions over sandpapergate on Friday [Getty Images] As Australian cricket captain Pat Cummins spent more than an hour being grilled by reporters over one of sport's biggest cheating scandals, the tension in the hall was occasionally pierced by muffled cheers. Outside, a crucial match in the top tier of domestic cricket was getting under way. Cummins was clear he'd rather we all be talking about that. But inside the nets at Cricket Central in Sydney, he faced more than a dozen TV cameras and a gaggle of journalists several times as large. His goal: to put rumours of his involvement in "sandpapergate" to rest. "I don't want to talk about this again after today," he said. "Even if it takes all day... I'll stay here until we have no more questions." A book by his friend and former teammate Usman Khawaja has renewed scrutiny on a 2018 plot to tamper with the ball using sandpaper in Australia's third Test match against South Africa in Cape Town. Three players admitted they were involved at the time and were handed lengthy bans, but in a memoir released last week, Khawaja said the entire Australian team knew about the sandpaper scheme. His claims have plunged the Australian cricket world into chaos, thrown speculation over key figures from that Test - including star bowler Cummins who has since risen to hold what many joke is Australia's most important job - and reopened wounds for fans. Josh, 28, told the BBC he thought everyone had moved on: "It's just a bit crazy that it's all blown up again... I think it is a bit ridiculous, after eight years." "I'm a bit bored of it," another spectator at the New South Wales vs South Australia Sheffield Shield match said. Josh says he was surprised the scandal is back in the news [BBC] Among fans, there's frustration that Khawaja has chosen to come forward now, almost a decade on and at the start of an exciting summer, and year, of cricket. Though there's an argument there'd never be a good time for Khawaja, who retired from international cricket in January, to make these allegations. There's worry about the impact on the men's team's performance this summer, after a lacklustre showing in South Africa last month - its first Test matches there since the 2018 incident. There's a sense of injustice that Australia can't escape the scandal, given - according to many players themselves - how common boundary-bending on ball tampering apparently was in that era. "It's a bit of a stitch up," 21-year-old James said. "Every country has done it... if it wasn't us, it was probably going to be someone else." Khawaja has said he owed it to the three players punished to tell his side of the story [Getty Images] Khawaja's memoir is also causing rancour among current and former players and coaches. In it, he said he had wanted the team to take collective responsibility for the tampering after batsman Cameron Bancroft was caught with the sandpaper on field. "I said: 'Take this as a team. We did this as a team. We knew what was going on, and we have to take it as a team'." However Khawaja has since said he didn't want to start a "witch hunt" and has refused to answer questions on exactly who he claims knew of the scheme, and what they knew. David Warner, who received the most severe punishment of the Cape Town trio, said Khawaja had written the truth and that Cummins' press conference denying the claims "threw him under the bus". Steve Smith, the captain at the time who was also suspended, has been travelling overseas and is yet to say anything publicly about the claims in the book. Bancroft is also staying silent for now despite previously suggesting the bowlers knew. But half of Australia's living cricket royalty and a slew of former coaches - some of whom have been accused of wrongdoing too - have thrown in their two cents. And Cricket Australia is under pressure from some to reopen its investigation into sandpapergate - something chief executive Todd Greenberg has already ruled out. Prof David Rowe of the University of Western Sydney told the BBC the saga was still so painful for many players and fans as the country sees itself as "a nation of good sports". "The idea of being a good sport is two things. One is being good at sport, so you actually win. But the other side is that you do it honourably and fairly," he said. "Many Australians would see themselves as above all that. That is: cheating is what other teams get up to... not the nation of good sports." He said the revelation was a "nasty shock" which brought the country "collective shame" which lingers today. He says he doubts that the cricket scene would be able to move on without a fresh response from the governing body, Cricket Australia. "One of the best ways to fuel conspiracy theories and keep sandpapergate going is to essentially say 'there's no more to see here' - especially when that comes from the authorities," Rowe said. Australia kicked off it's summer with an ODI against England on Friday [Getty Images] Asked about a fresh investigation, Cummins said it was a matter for Cricket Australia. Over the marathon press conference - which one reporter suggested was the longest in Australian sporting history - Cummins was cautious, pausing often to consider his responses and to make sure they answered the questions being asked of him. But he was also frank - using strong words to reject what he said were "vague" claims by Khawaja and admitting he was frustrated a friend had put him in this position. "Friends aren't casual with each other's lives and reputations... That's something I've been grappling with the last couple of days." As the reporters ran out of steam, Cummins said it was "annoying" that sandpapergate scandal was still a distraction for Australian cricket. He gestured outside to the Sheffield Shield match and mentioning Friday's one-day international against England in Perth, from which he and other key players are being rested. "It's been eight years... Hopefully today we put a line through it and we're done and we can all move on to much more fun topics, like actual cricket." Few people think he'll get his wish. "It's going to be hard to move on, given that there's two sides of the story and it doesn't look like either side is going to back down," James said. "I don't know what the outcome will be." 'Wrong' and 'nonsense' - Cummins on Khawaja claims Khawaja refuses to name Aussie ball tamperers

item.title: Joe Root scripts history against Australia, becomes only third England player to enter elite 200 list
item.description: England batting mainstay Joe Root on Friday became only the third player from the country to feature in 200 One-Day Internationals (ODIs). Root reached the milestone when he took the field for the first ODI against Australia at Perth Stadium. He joined Eoin Morgan, who played 225 ODIs, and Jos Buttler, who has 204 appearances, in the list of England players to reach the landmark. Australia captain Mitch Marsh won the toss and elected to bowl in the series opener, which comes amid renewed attention on the 2018 Sandpapergate scandal. Less than four hours before the toss, Australia Test captain Pat Cummins addressed a news conference in Sydney, dismissing claims made in Usman Khawaja’s autobiography, released this week, as “complete and utter nonsense.” Marsh said the opening ODI of the three-match series would be an important start to a busy 12 months for Australia, which includes a home Test series against New Zealand, tours of India and England, and next year's World Cup in South Africa. “It’s the start of the summer for us (and) that first game is always important,” he said. Australia will be without several of their first-choice fast bowlers for the white-ball series, with Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Scott Boland missing from the squad. Xavier Bartlett, left-arm pacer Spencer Johnson and 21-year-old Mahli Beardman are part of the bowling attack instead. Beardman, who hails from Western Australia, is making his international debut. Marsh said the young fast bowler would have a special occasion playing his first international match at home. “It’s going to be exciting for him. No better place in the world for a young West Australian to debut,” Marsh said. “We've got a reasonably young and inexperienced side, but lots of energy.” Australia are playing their first ODI since September, when they lost a three-match series 2-1 against South Africa. 135794817

item.title: Pochettino to take over at Manchester United; Grealish apologises to Everton fans: football – live
item.description: USMNT head coach is due to speak later on Friday Today’s fixtures | Follow us on TikTok | Mail David Mauricio Pochettino is expected to be appointed as the new Manchester United head coach later today. The Argentinian will leave his role with the United States to sign a two-and-a-half year contract at Old Trafford as Michael Carrick’s replacement. Carrick and his backroom staff were dismissed on Thursday, with Pochettino expected to bring his trusted lieutenants from previous roles with him. Friday 13 November: United are set to confirm his appointment. Saturday 14 November: He takes charge of the USA in the first leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final against Haiti in Miami (9.30pm UK time). Tuesday 17 November: He leads the USA for the last time, in the second leg against Haiti in Cincinnati (midnight UK time). Wednesday 18 November: He flies to Manchester to meet his new bosses. Thursday 19 November: He takes his first training session with the players. Sunday 22 November: His first game in charge is Liverpool away at Anfield (4.30pm). Gulp! Continue reading...

item.title: Tom Brady Ranks Chicago Bears Above Bills Despite Worse Record
item.description: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Tom Brady has placed the 7-2 Chicago Bears at the top of his latest NFL power rankings, even though the Buffalo Bills and San Francisco 49ers hold better records. The NFL legend explained his logic via Fox Sports after the Bears beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He noted that his list requires a team to lose a game to drop from the first spot. “Yeah and in my rankings, you got to lose to fall out of the top spot,” Brady said. The quarterback admitted that Caleb Williams made things difficult with four interceptions during the recent win, yet Chicago remains number one for now. Brady believes great teams must win ugly sometimes, pointing to how the defense created pressure all night long. He also highlighted Cairo Santos for coming up clutch to win the game in the final seconds. The Bye Week Question Brady paused to consider a specific scenario regarding the current schedule. The Bears have not lost since Williams returned from his injury, and now they get a bye week to clean things up. Brady wondered what happens to the number one team when they sit out a week. If the Bears remain inactive, Buffalo could surge to the summit, according to his suggestion that the door might be open. The Bills beat the Minnesota Vikings in Week 9 to earn their spot in second place. Per Yahoo Sports , the Jaguars took fifth place after going 6-2 following their win over the Baltimore Ravens. Within this specific ranking list, they stand as the sole team boasting six wins to reach the top five. The Denver Broncos hold fourth place at 7-2, while the 49ers come in at third after beating the Las Vegas Raiders. A report from Windy City Gridiron lists the San Francisco 49ers as the number one team, arguing they have been the league’s best since week one. That same source places the Chicago Bears at number two, noting they are the best team if every squad plays its best game. The report emphasizes that Chicago proved it can win even when it does not have its A game, as shown against Tampa. Player Performance and Midseason Awards The Bears are currently in their bye week after securing a 7-2 start to the year. According to Bear Goggles On , the team finds itself in first place in the NFC North despite some ups and downs. The source highlights defensive end Austin Booker as a key winner for the team this season. It also names Kyler Gordon as the Comeback Player of the Year after he racked up 13 tackles and four sacks in four games. Rookie Dillon Thieneman leads the Bears in tackles with 57, plus five pass deflections and two tackles for loss. The versatile weapon has shown a mix of linebacker and defensive back skills while Coby Bryant sits out. Despite an encouraging Week 9 showing versus the Buccaneers, Jaylon Johnson has allowed a 104.9 passer rating this year. item.title: Cowboys’ DeMarvion Overshown trending toward return vs. 49ers after injury update
item.description: Chris Jones-Imagn Images Cowboys’ DeMarvion Overshown trending toward return vs. 49ers after injury update appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . DeMarvion Overshown is looking for redemption after drawing a puzzling unsportsmanlike penalty during the Dallas Cowboys ’ Week 9 win versus the Indianapolis Colts, and it appears he will get the chance to earn it this Sunday against the San Francisco 49ers. The 2023 third-round draft pick is trending toward playing after posting full practice participation on Thursday, via Clarence Hill Jr. The Cowboys have a lengthy injury report, but it might get a little lighter come Friday. Overshown has dealt with hamstring and back injuries throughout the 2026 campaign and was inactive for the Colts game. That did not stop him from celebrating a big fumble recovery with his teammates on the field , a rule violation that cost Dallas 15 yards. The 26-year-old linebacker accepted responsibility for the mistake, but he probably still feels inclined to make a grand gesture on the gridiron. Forcing a turnover of his own or getting a big stop would probably suffice. Overshown has one interception, one forced fumble, 20 combined tackles and two passes defended in three games played. He is in the final year of his contract and is therefore running out of time to drive up his market value and wow executives. An impactful performance versus the 49ers, one of the current favorites to win Super Bowl 61, would surely help his cause. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) And it would breathe new life into the unsteady Cowboys. Dallas (4-5) can apply pressure to the New York Giants and pull within one game of first place in the NFC East. When in uniform, DeMarvion Overshown can be a positive presence for a run defense that is surrendering an NFC-worst 147.4 yards per week. Barring an unforeseen setback, he will line up opposite the 49ers (7-1) inside AT&T Stadium. The action will kick off at 4:25 p.m. ET. Related: 49ers’ George Kittle might wear his NSFW anti-Cowboys shirt in Week 10 clash Related: What Cowboys’ DeMarvion Overshown said about boneheaded penalty during Colts game

item.title: Will Ferguson-inspired Pochettino succeed where Carrick failed at Man Utd?
item.description: Maurucio Pochettino (right) was first mentioned as a contender to manage Manchester United when Louis van Gaal was sacked in May 2016 [Getty Images] When Mauricio Pochettino was asked the three Premier League managers he would have loved to have played for, he was unequivocal. "Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Alex Ferguson," replied Pochettino, who is set to be the next manager of Manchester United. In 2023, the Argentine - then at Chelsea, and dressed in full Blues training gear - was being interviewed by Sky Sports. Still he felt a need to express his adoration for Ferguson. Six years prior to that interview, while managing Tottenham, he had shared lunch with the legendary former United manager. "When I was young, when I started my career as a manager, he was always my inspiration, my reference," Pochettino said. "And when you can share two hours with a person who was the greatest manager in the history of football, you can only enjoy." Hiring United managers has been complicated since Ferguson's departure in 2013, and one of the most prominent complications has been a back-and-forth around the club's DNA. For some, winning by any means necessary should take precedence, while others believe the style of play and cultural heritage of United's most successful period is vital to the club's identity. In recent years, United's managerial merry-go-round has alternated between European coaches with their own fixed styles of play, and former players from the Ferguson era. But between his tactics of choice and his adoration for the former United boss, Pochettino may be uniquely placed to bridge the gap between both camps. Pochettino a decade in Man Utd's making - but Carrick deserves better Michael Carrick's United produced a series of good results to finish last season with a run unmatched by any other team in the league. They looked great, but it was a greatness built on attacking in a transition-heavy manner. Under Carrick, in games they had less than 50% of the ball, they only lost once. In those 13 games, they boasted a win-rate of 62%. This dropped to 36% in games they had the majority of possession. This style of play suited their direct attackers and protected their defenders. At the same time, Casemiro's set-piece prowess provided United a reliable way to break the deadlock against deep defences - something they have struggled with this season. With United a goal up, opponents stepped forward, giving Carrick's men more space. They could play to their strengths again, attacking quickly. It worked. But teams at the top are reluctant to play in this way. Carrick's vision for United was a side that played slick football, with short passes in build-up intuitively, referencing Paris St-Germain's midfield three as a source of inspiration. Building up in this manner, to entice and escape from pressure, before looking to find the forwards quickly, was the plan Carrick was working towards. "Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Alex Ferguson," replied Pochettino, who is set to be the next manager of Manchester United. In 2023, the Argentine - then at Chelsea, and dressed in full Blues training gear - was being interviewed by Sky Sports. Still he felt a need to express his adoration for Ferguson. Six years prior to that interview, while managing Tottenham, he had shared lunch with the legendary former United manager. "When I was young, when I started my career as a manager, he was always my inspiration, my reference," Pochettino said. "And when you can share two hours with a person who was the greatest manager in the history of football, you can only enjoy." Hiring United managers has been complicated since Ferguson's departure in 2013, and one of the most prominent complications has been a back-and-forth around the club's DNA. For some, winning by any means necessary should take precedence, while others believe the style of play and cultural heritage of United's most successful period is vital to the club's identity. In recent years, United's managerial merry-go-round has alternated between European coaches with their own fixed styles of play, and former players from the Ferguson era. But between his tactics of choice and his adoration for the former United boss, Pochettino may be uniquely placed to bridge the gap between both camps. Pochettino a decade in Man Utd's making - but Carrick deserves better Michael Carrick's United produced a series of good results to finish last season with a run unmatched by any other team in the league. They looked great, but it was a greatness built on attacking in a transition-heavy manner. Under Carrick, in games they had less than 50% of the ball, they only lost once. In those 13 games, they boasted a win-rate of 62%. This dropped to 36% in games they had the majority of possession. This style of play suited their direct attackers and protected their defenders. At the same time, Casemiro's set-piece prowess provided United a reliable way to break the deadlock against deep defences - something they have struggled with this season. With United a goal up, opponents stepped forward, giving Carrick's men more space. They could play to their strengths again, attacking quickly. It worked. But teams at the top are reluctant to play in this way. Carrick's vision for United was a side that played slick football, with short passes in build-up intuitively, referencing Paris St-Germain's midfield three as a source of inspiration. Building up in this manner, to entice and escape from pressure, before looking to find the forwards quickly, was the plan Carrick was working towards. This didn't come to fruition and trying to take United from a successful counter-attacking side to one that could reliably beat teams while keeping the ball was the same hurdle that undid Ole Gunnar Solskjar and Erik ten Hag. Former players under Sir Alex Ferguson, both Ole Gunnar Solskjar and Michael Carrick leaned into United’s historic style when crafting their game-models [Getty Images] Pochettino gives United an interesting solution to this problem. In his own words, he has described his sides as needing "to be protagonists, always press high, work hard and be dynamic". He refers to himself as a "disciple" of the legendary Argentina boss Marcelo Bielsa, who he played for. If you wanted an immediate comparison in the Premier League to a coach who resembles Pochettino's ideas in possession, it would be worth looking at Liverpool's Andoni Iraola, who similarly cites Bielsa as his reference. These are coaches who, while taking the initiative, encourage vertical football. For as different as the clubs are, both the fans of United and Liverpool have enjoyed success when their teams have played high-octane football. This summer's World Cup was a strong showcase of Pochettino's style of play and his recent tactical adaptation. Rather than a fixed, positional style of play - akin to the work of somebody like Manchester City's Enzo Maresca - Pochettino's USA had only certain players being tasked with holding their position. This approach posed problems for teams who defended in a zonal manner - defending specific areas rather than individual players. The US midfielders being able to move freely meant they could step into areas of the pitch between the zones that were being defended, which resulted in their players often being unmarked with time and space on the ball. By playing in close proximity to each other in the middle of the pitch, the US found another benefit. Small-space passing combinations helped draw the opposing team up towards the ball and combined with clever off-ball movement to stretch the pitch, allowed the US to find their striker with few defenders around him. Pochettino's men looked to thread through-balls in behind and early after enticing the opposition's press and the speedy Folarin Balogun was able to turn those chances into goals. This combination of a fluid midfield, small-space passing and direct through-balls doesn't sound dissimilar to what Carrick was trying to move towards implementing this season. And although that may worry United fans, the similarity in principles will benefit the players. "My philosophy is to give a freer style with a good organisation," were Pochettino's words in 2014. Although philosophically similar, that latter part - a clearer organisation to his freer style - is likely to be what Carrick was unable to reliably offer his players. For fans of top sides, fast-paced, vertical football tends to be accepted when it comes from a place of being proactive - think Ferguson's United or Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool - wanting to keep the ball, but not passing it for passing's sake. Fast-paced, vertical football tends to be frowned upon when it comes from a place of conceding possession and defending your own goal for long periods of the match. The first half of Carrick's stint did appear proactive, while his 4-2-4 press worked well. Leaving four players high was a risk that allowed them to win the ball back and score quickly, but as teams figured this out, United failed to adapt. There also appeared to be a drop in the team's fitness the longer United went from the departure of ex-boss Ruben Amorim, who left United well conditioned, albeit on the back of a schedule without European football. Here we see United's narrow 4-2-4 defensive shape in the first half against Como [Getty Images] Hiring Pochettino will immediately begin the process of turning United into a well-drilled side, capable of applying intense pressure, likely in a co-ordinated manner. Pochettino enjoyed relative success with Spurs, built on this intensity and co-ordination, that differentiated him from the rest of the league. With that unique selling point more common now than a decade ago, how he builds on it will dictate how his tenure unfolds. But watching Brighton this season, he can be assured that an approach founded on intensity off the ball can work in the Premier League in 2026, with Fabian Hurzeler's men second in the league, with the fourth highest average possession, 10 games in. Pochettino, from a footballing point of view, feels extremely aligned to the values of Ferguson's United, and as a result will implement numerous similarities to the things Carrick wanted, but ultimately failed, to deliver. His wealth of experience make him a more proven entity than the departing United manager and if he can get his team fit and pressing high, in typically Pochettino fashion, they should see an upturn in form. item.title: Texans special teams coach is pumped to play in ‘heavenly’ Cleveland weather
item.description: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Texans special teams coach is pumped to play in ‘heavenly’ Cleveland weather appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Unlike most players and coaches in the NFL, Houston Texans special teams coordinator Frank Ross relishes playing in inclement weather, as it adds another layer of gamesmanship. The Texans will visit the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on Sunday, and while some are worried about the windy forecast, Ross is not bothered at all, even though the Browns are still undefeated at home. When a reporter asked him about dealing with the “bad weather” in Cleveland, Ross had a quick counter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I call it good weather! That’s your opinion. I call it good weather! I think we are going to heaven,” said Ross in the video posted by The 33rd Team’s Ari Meirov. He then shared the Texans’ diligence in the challenging situation . “No matter when we go out there, we gotta have to test it. We gonna make sure we make those micro-adjustments relative to which end you’re kicking. Cleveland’s got two different ends. You have to know which way you’re going. To be able to make those and trust your line,” said Ross. #Texans STC Frank Ross on playing in Cleveland this week in “bad weather”: “I call it good weather! That’s your opinion. I call it good weather! I think we are going to heaven.” 😂😂 #FootballGuy pic.twitter.com/AyEMQHV6GS — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 12, 2026 He also expressed excitement for snapper Austin Brinkman, who could play a major role for Houston, as windy weather would deeply affect the offensive strategy of both squads. “Experience. That’s the only way you can improve in that. You gotta go in and do that,” added Ross. “We’ve got two snappers going against each other. They both played at the University of West Virginia. We’re gonna go handle the elements. We know they (Browns) can as well.” The Texans are coming off a win against the Los Angeles Chargers, 44-22, while the Browns are looking to snap a two-game skid. Related: Texans’ Will Anderson Jr. pops up on injury report before Browns game Related: Texans signs former Chiefs WR, return specialist for playoff push

item.title: 'Wrong' and 'nonsense' - Cummins on Khawaja claims
item.description: Pat Cummins was named Australia Test captain in 2021 [Getty Images] Australia captain Pat Cummins has hit back at former team-mate Usman Khawaja's claims over the sandpaper scandal, calling them "100% wrong" and "utter nonsense". In 2018, Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were punished for a plot to tamper with the ball using sandpaper in Australia's Test against South Africa in Cape Town. Khawaja has published his autobiography this week and the former batter has said the entire Australia team, which included Cummins, knew about the sandpaper scheme and should have taken responsibility. But in an extraordinary 68-minute address to the media in Sydney, Cummins countered and said: "When he says we all knew, if by that he means we knew sandpaper was going out on the field, he's 100% wrong. "I said that consistently for the last eight years. I did not know that was happening. "He says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball tamper with sandpaper. That's complete and utter nonsense." Cummins and Khawaja played 56 Tests together until Khawaja retired from international cricket in January. Khawaja was in the Australia XI when Cummins made his Test debut in 2011 and the pair were also once team-mates in domestic cricket with New South Wales. "Usman is a friend, but friends aren't casual with each other's lives and reputations," said Cummins. "In his book he's been casual with my life and the lives of many others - and, I think, Australian cricket. "I support him to tell his story, 100%, I'm glad he feels like he can, but we have to be accountable for the things that we say and do." In a media conference he arranged himself, Cummins began by promising to answer all questions because, he said: "I don't want to talk about this again after today." At times emotional, Cummins addressed a wide range of topics, including: Advice that some of Khawaja's claims are defamatory, but he will not take legal action He had been in contact with Khawaja and Smith since the book was published, but not Warner His belief that the one-year bans handed to Smith and Warner, and a nine-month suspension to Bancroft were "heavy handed" He had no recollection of Australia tampering with the ball in the 2017-18 Ashes series against England He had met with Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg, who has reviewed the files from the original investigation Explaining why sandpaper would have been present in the dressing room and that it was sometimes used by bowlers in training in order to practise with a reverse-swinging ball Khawaja's allegations have reopened the debate about the sandpaper plot, the investigation into the cheating, the culture of Australian cricket and the reputations of those involved. item.content:encoded: Pat Cummins was named Australia Test captain in 2021 [Getty Images] Australia captain Pat Cummins has hit back at former team-mate Usman Khawaja's claims over the sandpaper scandal, calling them "100% wrong" and "utter nonsense". In 2018, Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were punished for a plot to tamper with the ball using sandpaper in Australia's Test against South Africa in Cape Town. Khawaja has published his autobiography this week and the former batter has said the entire Australia team, which included Cummins, knew about the sandpaper scheme and should have taken responsibility. But in an extraordinary 68-minute address to the media in Sydney, Cummins countered and said: "When he says we all knew, if by that he means we knew sandpaper was going out on the field, he's 100% wrong. "I said that consistently for the last eight years. I did not know that was happening. "He says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball tamper with sandpaper. That's complete and utter nonsense." Cummins and Khawaja played 56 Tests together until Khawaja retired from international cricket in January. Khawaja was in the Australia XI when Cummins made his Test debut in 2011 and the pair were also once team-mates in domestic cricket with New South Wales. "Usman is a friend, but friends aren't casual with each other's lives and reputations," said Cummins. "In his book he's been casual with my life and the lives of many others - and, I think, Australian cricket. "I support him to tell his story, 100%, I'm glad he feels like he can, but we have to be accountable for the things that we say and do." In a media conference he arranged himself, Cummins began by promising to answer all questions because, he said: "I don't want to talk about this again after today." At times emotional, Cummins addressed a wide range of topics, including: Advice that some of Khawaja's claims are defamatory, but he will not take legal action He had been in contact with Khawaja and Smith since the book was published, but not Warner His belief that the one-year bans handed to Smith and Warner, and a nine-month suspension to Bancroft were "heavy handed" He had no recollection of Australia tampering with the ball in the 2017-18 Ashes series against England He had met with Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg, who has reviewed the files from the original investigation Explaining why sandpaper would have been present in the dressing room and that it was sometimes used by bowlers in training in order to practise with a reverse-swinging ball Khawaja's allegations have reopened the debate about the sandpaper plot, the investigation into the cheating, the culture of Australian cricket and the reputations of those involved. The story has dominated the media in Australia and caused headlines around the cricketing world. Khawaja has been supported by Warner and Chadd Sayers, a seam bowler who was part of the Australia squad on the 2018 tour of South Africa. However, his allegations have been rejected by Darren Lehmann, who was then the Australia head coach and former England batter Graeme Hick, one of Lehmann's assistants. Mitchell Starc, another bowler on the tour, has also denied Khawaja's claims. Khawaja has put a spotlight on Cummins and his fellow bowlers Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon. The four were Australia's attack in Cape Town and remain their first-choice bowlers eight years later. The quartet have always denied any knowledge of the plot, including in the release of a joint-statement in 2021. In his book - Sabr - Khawaja alleged Australia were urged to find ways of getting the ball to swing by a coach, while Bancroft was later encouraged to cheat. Khawaja also said he asked for the entire team to take responsibility for the controversy in Cape Town, but his request was rejected by two unnamed players. Cummins said he does not recall any suggestion that the team should have shared the responsibility, or that it was rejected. On the idea that the whole team were aligned in a plot to tamper with the ball, he said: "There was no masterplan around using illegal methods. People assume you've gone from very legal methods to suddenly taking sandpaper, and there must have been some huge masterplan. "That is not the case. There's no grand plan. There's no team meeting. There's no bowlers saying this is what must happen." "There's big leaps where Usman is being vague." In his book, Khawaja detailed how he was not interviewed as part of the investigation despite sitting next to Bancroft in the changing rooms during the Test at Newlands. Both Khawaja and Warner have criticised the investigation, which Greenberg has said he will not reopen. Cummins confirmed he has met with Greenberg and, although the captain said he did not want to break a "confidence", that Greenberg has reviewed the sandpaper files since the release of Khawaja's book and found the accounts in the investigation to be "consistent". Cummins has played 77 Tests for Australia and has been captain since 2021. He said he has seen only one instance of ball-tampering in his career, during a domestic Sheffield Shield match, when a player took a bottletop on to the field. However, he did admit that balls can sometimes be altered during training sessions, if bowlers want to practise in a certain way, or batters want to face a ball of a particular condition. Cummins said it was not unknown for training balls to be scuffed in such circumstances, using sandpaper or even a Stanley knife. When it was put to Cummins that he, as a bowler, must have suspected that the Cape Town ball had been tampered with, the 33-year-old described that bowlers often touch a ball as little as possible, in order to keep it dry and in a state where it will reverse-swing. At the time of the sandpaper scandal, Cummins was 24 and playing in his 13th Test. Asked about a potential culture of ball-tampering in that era, Cummins said he noticed things then that he now realises could have been cheating. On why Khawaja has chosen to speak now, at the end of his career, rather than in the intervening eight years, Cummins said the episode could have "weighed heavy" on the left-hander. Addressing the culture of the Australia team eight years ago, Cummins said: "I didn't like the way we spoke to umpires, the opposition. I think there was a bit of an arrogance and a bit of an ugliness at times that didn't sit well with me as a young guy. "Now I'm captain, I have spent a lot of time making sure that that's not the case." Speaking about Cummins' news conference on Fox Cricket, where he is working as an analyst for Australia's one-day series against England which got under way on Friday, Warner said: "I stick with Uzzie. It's the truth. The captain threw Uzzie under the bus. "We've got to live with the consequence daily. I feel it was a botched investigation. To get it over and done with. This won't rest. "I'm not going to accept [things] until the truth is out." Australian cricket's sandpapergate is back - and it cuts deep in a 'nation of good sports' Analysis - Cummins did not dodge a single question Khawaja's claims - in his book, in interviews and on social media - have re-opened old wounds in Australian cricket, drawing battle-lines that have verged on civil war. Over the past few days, constant questions have been asked of who knew what and if the truth has been covered up in the intervening eight years. The most pressure has been on the bowlers who played for Australia in Cape Town, none more so than Cummins, given his rise to the captaincy. He has been urged to front up, to show leadership. In an indoor cricket centre in Sydney, Cummins did just that. Others connected to the scandal who have faced the media in the past few days – Lehmann, Starc and Mitchell Marsh – have almost implicated themselves with vague responses to straight questions. Not Cummins. The captain did not duck or dodge any of the su

item.title: "You can't always play the same way for 90 minutes" – Zidane backs Olise after quiet second half against Italy
item.description: "You can't always play the same way for 90 minutes" – Zidane backs Olise after quiet second half against Italy Michael Olise struck early to capitalise on a mistake by Gianluigi Donnarumma and give France the lead in Thursday's UEFA Nations League clash against Italy. However, Olise's influence waned in the second half, as France struggled and ultimately suffered a 3-1 defeat. Speaking after the game, France coach Zinedine Zidane was unconcerned by Olise's drop in performance, arguing it's only natural that the winger cannot always play at the same level. He also pointed to the fact that the 24-year-old has scored five goals in his last five games for the national team. “You can’t always play the same way for 90 minutes. He has scored quite a few goals for us across the last two international breaks, and he has been very good. That’s what I’m focusing on,” Zidane said in defence of Olise at the post-match press conference, via RMC Sport. “I don’t think he was a little less effective in the second half. We were all a little less effective in the second half. And when the team isn’t playing as well, it affects individual performances.” Olise and France will be hoping to finish their UEFA Nations League Group A2 campaign with a win when they face Turkey on Sunday.

item.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
item.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? item.content:encoded: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. RELATED : Can the Ducks bounce back from UCLA loss? Experts release new Oregon vs. Nebraska predictions It’s not uncommon for teams with grand expectations to unravel in tough times. So far, that hasn’t happened. “The team is very connected and maintains its composure whether we’re winning or losing,” punter Bailey Ettridge said. “We haven’t let the losses last week and against Oklahoma State bring us down. I think we’ve handled them well.” Wide receiver Dakorien Moore said the team is filled with players who came to Oregon to win and be great. He added that the team’s goals remain attainable, and team leaders have worked to encourage togetherness and mutual trust. “If you can’t trust your teammate, then everything ain’t going to form in the way that it’s supposed to,” he said. This also means trusting the process, the plan and the team’s goal to get better instead of blaming one another. Oregon head coach Dan Lanning talks to the defense during a timeout as the No. 13 Oregon Ducks face the No. 21 UCLA Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian “Everybody knows what we want to attack this next week, being that Nebraska is a good team,” he said. The outside noise has been deafening. To say that many Oregon fans have melted down on social media would be an understatement. Virtually all of the players have social media accounts. Moore said he is active on social media but ignores negativity. Finney said he isn’t very active on social media and doesn’t care what people say outside the program. “Why would I let your opinion inflict me or my thoughts on my performance or my thoughts on our performance,” he said. “Because people are going to be there when you’re doing good, when you’re bad; when you’re doing bad, they’re going to leave you.” For that reason, the team lives by the motto F.E.B.U., which stands for “Forget Everyone But Us”. “F.E.B.U. is a true statement that we all follow,” Finney said. “… Just back to work. We got to figure out what we did wrong, go to the doctor, and just get back to work.” Fifth-year linebacker Devon Jackson said before the season that his main goal was team-driven — winning the national title. He is no longer looking that far ahead. “At the end of the year, what happens, happens, but I promise if we focus on the day and focus on one game at a time, we will be okay,” Jackson said. On Saturday, the Ducks’ defense played one of its best games of the season, while the offense played its worst without starting quarterback Dante Moore , who remains in concussion protocol. On teams that lack closeness, such a contrast can cause issues. But that is not the case with Oregon. “I mean, we’re all in this together,” Jackson said. “It’s not like, the defense won the game and offense lost, or special teams won or lost. We all lost together and we all win together. So, we got each other’s back no matter what.” Oregon offensive players celebrate a touchdown run by running back Jordon Davison (#0) as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 UCLA Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian Sean Meagher/The Oregonian Jackson said that after Saturday’s loss, he and senior center Iapani Laloulu talked for 20 minutes about the team. He told Laloulu that he didn’t care what was going on with the offense; the defense had its back. “I wouldn’t trade that group with anybody else in the country despite what other people may think,” Jackson said. “And we’re going to continue to lean on each other because it’s we all we got and we all we need.” Realistically, Oregon can’t expect much sympathy from outsiders. The Ducks have top-notch facilities, infinite uniform options, a roster with an estimated payroll of $50 million , and a coach who isn’t afraid to speak his mind, as Lanning did after beating the Trojans. Many in the football world certainly wouldn’t mind seeing Oregon fall. “Ain’t nobody going to feel sorry for us,” linebacker Matayo Uiagalelei said. “So just came back in the next day with the mindset ready to work.” . . . item.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. Michigan State Spartans defensive back Charles Brantley (4) tackles Illinois Fighting Illini wide receiver Collin Dixon (17) in a Big 10 football game at Spartan Stadium in East Lansing, Mich. on Saturday, October 10, 2026. Isaac Ritchey | iritchey@mlive

item.title: Oregon QB Dante Moore ruled out for rest of 2026 season
item.description: Oregon Ducks quarterback Dante Moore will miss the rest of the season, coach Dan Lanning announced Monday night. “I’m not anticipating him being back this season,” Lanning said. “Really got clarity for us this past week, for him,” Lanning added. “And I think if it were up to Dante in any shape, way, he would want to be out there playing for the guys. But, unfortunately, it’s not really up to Dante. It’s not really up to me. We can control the setting and practice where he’s able to do things for us, but that’s not always the case in the game.” Lanning said he expects Moore, who has run scout-team offense in practice, to fully recover. “That hasn’t changed,” Lanning said. “Definitely feel that way, but for him to be out there on the field for us right now, that’s not gonna happen.” Lanning added that Moore would remain involved with the team. “He’s still going to be a big part of this team and helping us move forward and find opportunities for us to be better,” Lanning said. Watch " Oregon Ducks QB Dante Moore to miss remainder of 2026 season " on YouTube Watch The announcement comes days after the reeling Ducks lost 21-10 at Illinois on Saturday in the third straight game Moore missed while in concussion protocol. Before the Illinois game, Moore told The Oregonian/OregonLive that he felt good but didn’t know if he’d return this season and was taking it “one day at a time.” “That’s all I can do,” he said. item.content:encoded: Oregon Ducks quarterback Dante Moore will miss the rest of the season, coach Dan Lanning announced Monday night. “I’m not anticipating him being back this season,” Lanning said. “Really got clarity for us this past week, for him,” Lanning added. “And I think if it were up to Dante in any shape, way, he would want to be out there playing for the guys. But, unfortunately, it’s not really up to Dante. It’s not really up to me. We can control the setting and practice where he’s able to do things for us, but that’s not always the case in the game.” Lanning said he expects Moore, who has run scout-team offense in practice, to fully recover. “That hasn’t changed,” Lanning said. “Definitely feel that way, but for him to be out there on the field for us right now, that’s not gonna happen.” Lanning added that Moore would remain involved with the team. “He’s still going to be a big part of this team and helping us move forward and find opportunities for us to be better,” Lanning said. Watch " Oregon Ducks QB Dante Moore to miss remainder of 2026 season " on YouTube Watch The announcement comes days after the reeling Ducks lost 21-10 at Illinois on Saturday in the third straight game Moore missed while in concussion protocol. Before the Illinois game, Moore told The Oregonian/OregonLive that he felt good but didn’t know if he’d return this season and was taking it “one day at a time.” “That’s all I can do,” he said. He then began throwing passes on the field in shorts and a sweatshirt. Saturday’s loss all but knocked Oregon (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) out of the national playoff picture and led Lanning to fire offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer on Sunday. Without Moore, Oregon scored 42 points over three games and lost twice while rotating between backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Moore was injured on Sept. 26 at USC while sliding to end a 10-yard run to the USC 13-yard line. As Moore began to slide, Trojans linebacker Desman Stephens II hit him in the head with his shoulder. Oregon quarterback Dante Moore, center bottom, takes a hard tackle by lSouthern California inebacker Desman Stephens II, center top, during the first half of an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Sept. 26, 2026, in Los Angeles. (AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill) AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill Moore was taken off the field in a cart and loaded into an ambulance. Following Moore’s injury, Raiola entered the game and led the Ducks to a 41-27 win. Moore entered the concussion protocol but returned to practice the following bye week. Speculation was that Moore would return once he cleared the protocols. But each subsequent availability report listed Moore as out. On Oct. 10, Oregon lost 17-15 to UCLA, with Raiola struggling through three quarters before being replaced in the fourth quarter by Thomas. Thomas started the following week against Nebraska, but he played poorly before Raiola entered the game in the fourth quarter and led the Ducks to a 17-14 comeback win. Oregon’s realistic national playoff hopes remained alive at 4-2 — until the loss to Illinois. At 4-3, the Ducks must win their final five games to reach 9-3 and hope enough playoff contenders finish with three losses so the Ducks can receive a berth. If Moore enters the 2027 NFL Draft, his announcement will end his brief Ducks career, during which he led the program to one of its best seasons. Oregon quarterback Dante Moore walks off the field after the No. 5 Ducks fall to the No. 1 Indiana Hoosiers, 56-22, in the Peach Bowl at the College Football Playoff semifinals from Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta on Friday, Jan. 9, 2025. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian Sean Meagher/The Oregonian Lanning said he wasn’t sure what Moore’s plans were after this season. “That’s not fair for me to say or speculate,” Lanning said. “Obviously, he’ll have a decision again at the end of the season and what that looks like. I think we all can acknowledge that Dante is a great player and he will get an opportunity to get drafted. But what that looks like in the future, I think that’s a decision for a later date. I don’t know where his mind is at on that. We haven’t had a conversation. That’s not where my focus is at. I don’t think that’s where his focus is at right now. There’s a reason you get time to make that decision later on.” Moore committed to Oregon in the summer of 2022. Later, he flipped to UCLA in December of 2022 rather than back up Ducks quarterback Bo Nix in 2023. That summer, Moore learned that his mother had been diagnosed with cancer, adding to the pressure he was feeling while trying to perform as a highly touted freshman. Moore had a rough freshman season at UCLA. His midseason struggles led Chip Kelly to bench Moore. Following the season, Moore entered the transfer portal and committed to the Ducks in December 2023. Moore transferred to Oregon to develop while backing up the team’s new starter, Oklahoma transfer Dillon Gabriel. That plan paid off in 2025. Moore passed for 3,565 yards, 30 touchdowns and 10 interceptions while leading the Ducks to a 13-2 record and the playoff semifinals, where they lost to eventual national champion Indiana. Moore, a projected first-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, returned to Oregon for his senior season to keep improving with a team that returned eight defensive starters and was expected to contend for a national championship. Oregon quarterback Dante Moore (#5) celebrates with running back Tradarian Ball (#4) after Ball’s touchdown as the No. 21 Ducks face the Portland State Vikings in a non-conference college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Friday, Sept. 18, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian Oregon entered the season ranked No. 2 — the highest preseason ranking in program history — and defeated Boise State, 34-27, in the opener. Moore passed for a career-high 378 yards with three touchdown passes. The season began to unravel the following week when the heavily favored Ducks lost 39-31 at Oklahoma State. The following week, Oregon won 84-0 over Portland State. Next came the USC game. The Ducks, who host No. 20 Northwestern (6-1, 3-1), could continue to start Raiola or turn to former four-star recruit Akili Smith Jr. Chances are, Lanning will go with whichever quarterback he believes can win games. In the offseason, Oregon is expected to seek a quarterback in the transfer portal. With high expectations at Oregon, Lanning likely won’t bank on Raiola or Smith as the starter in 2027. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. Oregon Ducks QB Dylan Raiola (8) throws a pass to Oregon Ducks RB Dierre Hill Jr. (6) during a college football game between the Oregon Ducks and Illinois Fighting Illini on October 24, 2026 at Gies Memorial Stad
