Oregon Ducks QB Dylan Raiola (8) throws a pass to Oregon Ducks RB Dierre Hill Jr. (6) during a college football game between the Oregon Ducks and Illinois Fighting Illini on October 24, 2026 at Gies Memorial Stadium in Champaign, IL. (Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire) (Icon Sportswire via AP Images) AP Raiola avoided throwing anyone under the bus but acknowledged what the question implied. Passing games are built on timing. If the quarterback can’t fully trust the receivers running the routes, synergy suffers and efficiency wanes. That’s less a knock on the receivers than an acknowledgment that it’s easier to develop a connection with a team’s more polished top receivers than with those thrust into action by circumstance. At times, running back Dierre Hill Jr. played wide receiver alongside freshmen Hudson Lewis and Gatlin Bair. Neither had played much until injuries hit the group. Lanning said Stewart would return. McClellan is out indefinitely. 5. The failed gadget play Much has been made about the failed gadget play in the third quarter. Many have blamed Mehringer for the play-call and the negative result hurting momentum. Let’s examine. Oregon trailed 14-10, forced an Illinois punt and took over at the Ducks’ 9-yard line. Five plays later, Oregon moved the ball to its 47. That’s when the gadget play came out. Oregon lined up with four offensive linemen to the far left, with wide receiver Dakorien Moore behind the linemen. Three Illinois defenders lined up on that side with a fourth closer to the box. Raiola checked to a run play and handed the ball to Moore on a jet sweep to the right, where the Ducks were outnumbered. The poorly-blocked play resulted in a one-yard loss. A couple of plays later, Oregon punted. After the game, Lanning was asked whether the failed play hurt the team at that moment. “Yeah, it’s a great question,” he said. “It certainly wasn’t successful. There’s a pause in operation there, right?” Yes, but who is at fault for the failed play? Is it Raiola for reading it wrong and not passing to Moore? Is it Mehringer for calling the play? Or is it Lanning for allowing the play to happen? For that play to be called, it must be accepted by Lanning, practiced, reviewed on film and further stamped by Lanning to appear on the play sheet. Then, when Mehringer calls it, Lanning must let it go through. He can hear every play call through the coaches’ headsets. If Lanning didn’t like the play, he could have vetoed it. He did not. The concept is not much different from when Lanning chooses to go for two after touchdowns. If Oregon gets the favorable look it wants, it takes the shot. That’s what happened with the gadget play. But Oregon made the wrong choice and the play failed. Regardless of the process, had Lanning not liked the play, he could have stopped it from being called. 6. Oregon’s rushing attack came to life Oregon gained 180 yards on the ground against a team that ranked 12th in the Big Ten in rushing defense, allowing 134.4 yards per game. CHAMPAIGN, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 24: Jordon Davison #0 of the Oregon Ducks scores a touchdown against Matthew Bailey #7 of Illinois during the first half at Memorial Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Champaign, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) Getty Images Still, too many drives started well before getting stuffed, putting more pressure on Raiola, who couldn’t consistently deliver. As a result, Oregon converted on just four of 15 third-down attempts. With most of the team’s top receivers out, the rushing attack needed to be special, and it wasn’t. 7. Tough day for kicker Gage Hurych The junior entered the game 9-for-9 on field-goal attempts and went 1-for-4. But two of his three misses came from beyond 50 yards. Hurych missed his first attempt from 52 yards out. He made a 20-yard field goal in the second quarter to put Oregon up 10-0. He missed a 53-yarder with 6:04 to go in the fourth quarter and later missed a 47-yarder with 52 seconds to go. “He’s human,” Lanning said. “The reality is, those are long kicks. Some of those are really tough. The wind’s a little bit different in this stadium. I think we put them in a position that wasn’t the easiest to operate, and we’ve been really fortunate this year.” 8. Rushing defense faltered when it mattered most. Oregon’s defense kept the Ducks in the games against UCLA and Nebraska until the offense started to come alive. Oregon lost to the Bruins 17-15 and beat Nebraska 17-14. On Saturday, the Ducks led 10-0 late in the second quarter. At that point, nobody knew Oregon wouldn’t score again. But the defense’s job was to keep dominating, just in case. Illinois Fighting Illini RB Aidan Laughery (21) runs the ball into the end zone for a touchdown during a college football game between the Oregon Ducks and Illinois Fighting Illini on October 24, 2026 at Gies Memorial Stadium in Champaign, IL. (Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It failed. Illinois running back Aidan Laughery got loose for a 75-yard touchdown run, making it 10-7 with 2:15 left in the half. Illinois had rushed for just 14 yards before that run, b

item.content:encoded: A new head coach will roam the sidelines. A franchise icon will make his long-awaited return. An All-Star will begin his redemption tour. And a new ownership group will watch its first season opener from Paul Allen’s former seats along the Moda Center baseline. The Blazers open the 2026-27 NBA season Wednesday night against the Phoenix Suns — a team they upset in April in the play-in tournament — and if you’re just now tuning in for the start of the regular season, well, there’s a lot you missed. RELATED: Suns vs. Blazers predictions, odds and best bets: Dame is home, and the model likes Portland on opening night Let’s catch you up. What does the starting lineup look like? The Blazers are expected to unveil a new starting lineup that features a pair of notable All-Star additions: Damian Lillard and Ja Morant . The backcourt duo is joining a fivesome that includes returning starters Deni Avdija , Toumani Camara and Donovan Clingan . It’s a versatile, star-studded lineup that features three All-Stars, a former All-Defensive Second Team selection, one of the best young centers in the NBA and loads of scoring potential. What about the rotation? Micah Nori , the Blazers’ first-year head coach, said he plans on using a 10-man rotation to start the season, which will allow the Blazers to capitalize on their depth and versatility. In addition to the starters, Jrue Holiday, Scoot Henderson, Sidy Cissoko, Robert Williams III and Vit Krejci are expected to open the season in the rotation. The group could change depending on matchups and Williams’ availability — he did not play in back-to-backs last season — and it’s likely that Micah Potter, Branden Carlson and Yang Hansen will occasionally see spot duty, as well. Wait … the Blazers have a new coach? The Blazers stabilized their turbulent coaching situation in June, hiring longtime NBA assistant Nori to replace interim coach Tiago Splitter . Nori, who interviewed for head coaching jobs seven times before finally landing his first chance, is entering his 29th season in the league and is universally revered in NBA circles for his positive approach, ability to connect with players and sharp basketball mind. Early indications have been encouraging, as the Blazers players seem to love him and the front office works well with him. The Blazers’ coaching position had been embroiled in controversy, of course, as former coach Chauncey Billups — who was placed on indefinite leave by the NBA — is facing federal felony charges related to money laundering and wire fraud conspiracy for his alleged involvement in a rigged underground poker game. What style will the Blazers play? In a stark contrast to recent seasons, the Blazers are constructed around their offense rather than their defense. The roster is unbalanced, featuring five dynamic ball-handlers and playmakers (Lillard, Morant, Avdija, Holiday and Henderson), a solid center combination (Clingan and Williams) and little wing depth. As a result, the team is expected to play fast and free under Nori, bringing lots of speed, passing, cutting and flow. Nori said he hopes to rotate his players liberally in shorter shifts during games — perhaps as short as three minutes — which will enable them to play with maximum effort before giving way to teammates. The interior defense is strong with Clingan and Williams patrolling the middle, Camara remains one of the NBA’s best and most versatile defenders and Cissoko will be asked to guard one-through-five. Holiday is still capable of locking down opposing guards and Avdija has pledged to be more of a two-way threat now that he doesn’t have to serve as the team’s primary ball-handler. But the backcourt combination of Morant and Lillard, while lethal on offense, is not imposing on defense and relatively small (both stand 6-foot-2). What are the Blazers’ expectations? Portland defied pundits last season, winning 10 of its last 14 regular season games to secure a spot in the play-in tournament, where it beat the Suns in Phoenix to earn the seventh seed in the Western Conference. The San Antonio Spurs dismissed the Blazers with a gentleman’s sweep in the playoffs , but the strong run — combined with the additions of Lillard and Morant — has raised expectations in Portland. How much? Camara said in training camp that the Blazers’ goal is to win 50 or more games and secure home-court advantage in the postseason. It won’t be easy. The league is as deep and talented as ever, and new rules surrounding the lottery should discourage teams from tanking, meaning most of the league will be chasing wins instead of lottery ping-pong balls late into the season. It seemed like a third of the league had given up last year by the All-Star break. Latest Blazers news Joe Freeman’s 3 takeaways from the Trail Blazers’ back-to-back sweep vs. Thunder Trail Blazers lose rotation player for 2 months Joe Freeman’s 3 takeaways from Trail Blazers’ rout over the Thunder Thunder vs. Blazers predictions: Portland looks to snap two-game skid in the first of back-to-back meetings Joe Freeman’s 3 takeaways from Trail Blazers’ lopsided loss to Spurs Early-season schedule is a doozy As the Blazers’ new-look lineup works to build chemistry and a first-year coach settles into a new role, the schedule will be challenging. Six of the first eight games — and 12 of the first 17 — will come on the road and include a slew of playoff contenders, including the Spurs, Oklahoma City Thunder (twice), Minnesota Timberwolves (twice), New York Knicks, Philadelphia 76ers, Denver Nuggets and Los Angeles Lakers (twice). But what about Dame? The most uplifting part of opening night figures to be the return of Lillard, the franchise icon who is back after spending two seasons in Milwaukee and one season on the injured list. The nine-time All-Star and franchise leader has not played in an NBA regular-season or playoff game since April 27, 2025, when he suffered a torn left Achilles tendon. And he has not played with Portland since March 22, 2023, six months before it traded him to the Bucks. Lillard showed no ill effects from his injury during the exhibition season, when he played in three of the Blazers’ four games and averaged 17.3 points, 2.7 assists and 22.7 minutes. If anything, he looked like the same old Dame, swishing three-pointers, creating off the dribble, initiating offense and drawing defensive attention. Lillard joked earlier this week that he’s “not an old man,” but also acknowledged that he isn’t likely to play upward of 38 minutes a game like he used to and may even take a night off here and there for rest, most likely on a random back-to-back. His addition not only should help cover up two of the Blazers’ biggest weaknesses last season — three-point shooting and shooting in the clutch — but also inspire a thirsty fan base, which has rarely loved a player more. All the while, Lillard says he intends to play with more “joy” than ever. Read the original article on oregonlive.com . Add oregonlive.com as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. They’re confident they can challenge any defense vertically. “The underneath throws are going to be there,” Hampton said. “We got the best OC in the country; we’re going to be able to go deep if we want to.” Latest Beavers news Oregon State QB Braden Atkinson going through further testing of hand injury before Boise State game Oregon State basketball lands 3-star center for 2027 class Oregon State wome

item.title: Report: €100m-rated Brighton defender dreams of Real Madrid move despite Liverpool interest
item.description: Report: €100m-rated Brighton defender dreams of Real Madrid move despite Liverpool interest Luka Vuskovic has reportedly identified Real Madrid as his ultimate career destination, potentially complicating Liverpool’s pursuit of the Brighton and Hove Albion defender. According to Sky Sport Germany journalist Florian Plettenberg , Liverpool have placed the 19-year-old on their shortlist for next summer, but the Croatian’s long-term ambition is to play at the Santiago Bernabeu. Vuskovic has made an impressive start to life at Brighton following his move from Tottenham in July. Understandably, his performances have attracted attention across Europe, with the Premier League club now in a strong position to demand a substantial fee for one of its most promising young players. Liverpool interest grows as Vuskovic establishes himself at Brighton Plettenberg reports that Liverpool are monitoring Vuskovic regularly as they assess their defensive options ahead of the summer 2027 transfer window. Luka Vuskovic dreams of playing for Real Madrid one day. (Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images) The centre-back has firmly established himself under Fabian Hurzeler, strengthening his reputation after an impressive loan spell at Hamburger SV. Brighton signed him this past summer for a reported £46 million, with a further £4 million in achievable add-ons. The Croatian agreed a five-year contract running until 2031, and there is no release clause that would allow an interested club to bypass negotiations. Real Madrid are his dream destination Despite Liverpool’s interest, Vuskovic’s long-term ambition is to represent Real Madrid one day. Notably, he is very happy with his development at Brighton, meaning there is no immediate indication that he wants to leave. Liverpool are closely monitoring Luka Vuskovic. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images) However, if he does push for an exit, Brighton are understood to value him at around €100 million, a figure that would be a significant increase on their initial investment. Real Madrid will undergo defensive overhaul If Real Madrid are linked with the player in future, it would ideally make sense given their ongoing efforts to build a younger defensive core. Ibrahima Konate joined the club this summer, while Jacobo Ramon has emerged as a possible longer-term option following his development at Como. However, reports suggest Real Madrid have yet to make a final decision on bringing Ramon back. Furthermore, with Antonio Rudiger potentially in his final season, the team will indeed need a new centre-back, leaving Vuskovic as a potentially attractive future target, although the financial implications would be considerable.

item.title: Carlo Ancelotti delivers positive Raphinha update amid Barcelona fitness concerns: ‘Doing very well’
item.description: Carlo Ancelotti delivers positive Raphinha update amid Barcelona fitness concerns: ‘Doing very well’ Carlo Ancelotti has offered an encouraging assessment of Raphinha’s condition ahead of Brazil’s friendly against Japan, confirming that the Barcelona forward is doing well with both club and country. His comments come as Barcelona monitor the winger’s workload during the November international break, with the Catalan club keen to avoid another physical setback after his recent return from injury. Raphinha, who will captain the national team , has travelled to Singapore for Brazil’s two friendlies, against Japan on November 14 and Singapore on November 17. The number of minutes he receives there will be an important consideration for Barcelona, given his value to Hansi Flick and the injuries that have disrupted his recent availability. Ancelotti praises Raphinha’s form and versatility Speaking at his pre-match press conference, Ancelotti offered a positive assessment of the Barcelona forward’s current condition and performances. Raphinha will captain the national team during November friendlies. (Photo by Ian Hitchcock/Getty Images) “Raphinha is doing very well here and at Barcelona. He’s showing impressive quality at Barça and can play as a striker,” said the former Real Madrid boss, according to AS . Raphinha’s fitness remains an important consideration following his recent muscular problems. As stated earlier, Barcelona and the Brazilian Football Confederation have coordinated to manage his involvement during the two friendlies, reducing the risk of another setback. However, it is crucial to note that no specific minutes limit has been publicly confirmed. Meanwhile, Ancelotti also addressed the players’ motivation to represent their country, something that was questioned after Raphinha’s comments during his contract renewal , stressing the importance of Brazil’s status and the support they receive from their fans. Ancelotti confirms Raphinha is motivated to play for Brazil. (Photo by Albert Perez/Getty Images) “I know the players want to play for the national team and I don’t need to say anything to them to get them out there competing. “Brazil is the greatest national team in the world and the fans will be right behind us in every match and will support us. It’s different in other countries.” Flick will be hoping Raphinha returns without another setback For Barcelona, it is quite clear that they will want their captain to complete international duty in good condition. Raphinha’s pressing, attacking output and leadership make him an important part of Flick’s plans, leaving the club with little incentive to take unnecessary risks with his fitness. Brazil, meanwhile, have their own reasons to use him carefully. Ancelotti knows the forward is an important attacking option, and managing his minutes will be crucial even for him, as these two matches are mere friendlies.

item.title: Record-breaking Harry Kane sees Luka Modrić’s career as an inspiration
item.description: England fans hold up a tifo featuring England's Harry Kane, marking his Ballon d'Or triumph and his achievement in becoming England's all-time record appearance holder with 126 appearances, ahead of the UEFA Nations League match between England vs Croatia at Wembley Stadium. (is associated with: «Record-breaking Harry Kane sees Luka Modrić’s career as an inspiration») John Walton/PA Wire/dpa Harry Kane vowed to “push the limits” like inspirational 41-year-old Luka Modrić following his record-breaking England appearance against Croatia. The 33-year-old enjoyed a night to remember at a sold-out Wembley on Thursday, when a giant tifo hailed ‘England’s finest’ as the captain led the team for his landmark 126th cap. Kane was given a rapturous reception and displayed the Ballon d’Or to the crowd before a series of presentations centred on him setting a new England’s men’s appearance record. The Prince of Wales, William, and previous record holder Peter Shilton led the celebrations on a night that ended with the skipper’s spot-kick sealing a 2-1 Nations League win against Croatia under the arch. “It was incredible, just everything was amazing,” said Kane, who admitted he was “trying to play it cool” when he walked out to see a giant banner recognizing his 126th cap. “A big thank you to everyone who organized it here at the FA, with the tifo and presentations. Thank you to Luka (Modrić) and the Croatian organization for their gift as well. “Obviously I knew there was going to be something before the game and it was just a special moment. “It’s been a crazy few weeks with a lot happening and of course it’s an important moment in our history as a national team, so you have to enjoy these moments. “But then once the game started, it was just full focus on that. “I’ve said before, these occasions feel much better when you win and obviously now I can take a breath and enjoy the whole night itself.” Kane was on the Wembley pitch long after the final whistle with friends and family, who will have undoubtedly further significant moments to celebrate in the years to come. The striker is now just eight international goals shy of joining the 100 club and plans to play for England until the wheels come off, with fellow Ballon d’Or winner Modrić's longevity providing motivation. (is associated with: «Record-breaking Harry Kane sees Luka Modrić’s career as an inspiration») John Walton/PA Wire/dpa Harry Kane vowed to “push the limits” like inspirational 41-year-old Luka Modrić following his record-breaking England appearance against Croatia. The 33-year-old enjoyed a night to remember at a sold-out Wembley on Thursday, when a giant tifo hailed ‘England’s finest’ as the captain led the team for his landmark 126th cap. Kane was given a rapturous reception and displayed the Ballon d’Or to the crowd before a series of presentations centred on him setting a new England’s men’s appearance record. The Prince of Wales, William, and previous record holder Peter Shilton led the celebrations on a night that ended with the skipper’s spot-kick sealing a 2-1 Nations League win against Croatia under the arch. “It was incredible, just everything was amazing,” said Kane, who admitted he was “trying to play it cool” when he walked out to see a giant banner recognizing his 126th cap. “A big thank you to everyone who organized it here at the FA, with the tifo and presentations. Thank you to Luka (Modrić) and the Croatian organization for their gift as well. “Obviously I knew there was going to be something before the game and it was just a special moment. “It’s been a crazy few weeks with a lot happening and of course it’s an important moment in our history as a national team, so you have to enjoy these moments. “But then once the game started, it was just full focus on that. “I’ve said before, these occasions feel much better when you win and obviously now I can take a breath and enjoy the whole night itself.” Kane was on the Wembley pitch long after the final whistle with friends and family, who will have undoubtedly further significant moments to celebrate in the years to come. The striker is now just eight international goals shy of joining the 100 club and plans to play for England until the wheels come off, with fellow Ballon d’Or winner Modrić's longevity providing motivation. The 41-year-old extended his Croatian appearance record to 207 after coming off the bench at Wembley, where England fans gave him a warm reception. “He’s an inspiration for a lot of us,” Kane said. “What an incredible player, but what a great person as well and someone who’s looked after himself. “A great professional and to be playing 40, 41 now, still at this level, is credit to all of his hard work and his mentality. “So, yeah, that inspires me to push the limits. Like with him, I think you just keep going to see how far your body takes you, your mentality takes you. “Everyone’s journey is different for sure but I’ve said before that as long as I feel like I can help the national team, as long as I feel like I’m performing at the highest level, then I’ll be here for as long as I can. “Whether that’s until I’m 40 or not, we’ll have to wait and see. But right now, yeah, I’ve enjoyed every moment.” Kane’s immediate attention is on England’s final fixture of the year against World Cup winners Spain in Madrid, where they head having rubberstamped progress to the Nations League quarter-finals. Thomas Tuchel’s side lost 3-2 to Wembley in the Group A3 opener but four straight wins since then gives them hope of finishing top of the pool on Sunday. “There were things that we can improve on, but it was just about getting the win ultimately,” Kane added. “It sets up a fantastic game on Sunday now.”

item.title: Coco Gauff Clears The Air About ‘Stupid’ WTA Finals Rules Complaint After Backlash
item.description: Coco Gauff. © IMAGN Coco Gauff addressed the backlash surrounding her recent comments about the WTA Finals format. Gauff started her run in Indian Wells with a 6-4, 6-7 (5), 6-2 win over compatriot Jessica Pegula. However, she fell in the next round to Linda Noskova, who beat her 6-3, 6-3. The defeat made her advancement in the semifinal round uncertain. Her qualification not only depended on her match against Marta Kostyuk, but also on Pegula’s clash against Linda Noskova. After her second loss, Gauff appeared to express frustration with WTA qualification. Later, following her third-round match against Kostyuk, she was asked to address her previous statement. Gauff clarified that she wasn’t calling the format stupid; rather, she meant that thinking about different qualification scenarios while playing a match would be foolish. “Can I clear that up? Okay. I wasn’t saying the format was stupid. I was saying if you get in if you get like in your head while you’re playing into all the scenarios that’s stupid. But of course, everyone thought I was calling the format [laughter] stupid. But I was trying to because he asked me, ‘Am I gonna look at the different scenarios and stuff,’ and I was trying to say like no, if I like play while thinking about the scenarios it’s stupid because it’s tennis. Like you can’t, ‘Oh, I want to win this match in straight sets.’ Every match you want to win in straight sets.” Despite seeing off Marta Kostyuk, Coco Gauff saw her pursuit come to an end as Jessica Pegula finished in second place in Group 1 after dominating Linda Noskova 7-6(2), 4-6, 7-5. Coco Gauff opens up about the hot mic controversy at the WTA Finals involving her, Mirra Andreeva and Jessica Pegula Coco Gauff recently opened up about the hot mic incident at the WTA Finals, where Jessica Pegula was heard making statements about her compatriot and Mirra Andreeva. Pegula slammed Andreeva, calling her a ‘diva’ who ‘needed to be humbled.’ She also criticized Andreeva’s coach, Conchita Martinez, for putting up with her behavior. Pegula also compared Andreeva and Gauff, saying Andreeva could be a better player and surpass Gauff if she had Gauff’s mentality. During the event, Gauff addressed the incident, stating that she had no grudges with Pegula. “Jess, she told me, before I even saw the video, she came and apologized immediately,” Gauff said. “Honestly, I didn’t really take it. I feel like maybe the other person in the situation got a lot more of it. But she, you know, they both, even her coach, apologized to me. So yeah, I think for me, I’m a competitor, so I’m always going to compete regardless of what’s happening off the court. But yeah, I know her heart, and it was all good. I don’t feel any type of way.” Jessica Pegula will lock horns with Mirra Andreeva in the semifinals of the WTA Finals. item.title: Chicago Bears Win Despite Historic Mess Against Tampa Bay
item.description: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images The Chicago Bears made history on Sunday night by winning a game despite committing five turnovers, taking nine penalties, and failing to rush for a single 10‑yard gain. Yahoo Sports noted this odd mix of errors and victory makes the team look different than any other squad in the league this season. No other team in NFL history has ever blown a 14-point lead at home, taken so many penalties, and still secured a win against a team like Tampa Bay. Bears head coach Ben Johnson admitted the team did not play their best football during the 27-24 victory over the Buccaneers on Sunday, Nov. 8. He told reporters that while the win is what matters most right now, the style of play leaves room for growth. “At the end of the day, that’s the end goal that we’re looking for,” Johnson said, referring to the victory itself. He also noted that the players in the locker room knew they had underperformed even though they got the win. A Team Finding Its Grit Johnson felt a specific energy from the group despite the sloppy stats, which he called a positive sign for the future. “I felt that from our crew, which is a good thing,” Johnson said. The team now sits at 7-2 as they head into their bye week, giving them time to fix the issues that plagued them against Tampa Bay. The coach said good teams can win without playing their A‑game. Key players like linebacker Devin Bush and edge rusher Austin Booker stepped up when the offense struggled to move the ball. Johnson commended Bush for delivering a top-tier performance as a Chicago Bear, a sight that was remarkable. He further emphasized Booker’s intensity and effort, observing that the defensive players continue improving week in and week out. These individual efforts helped the team overcome the five turnovers and the loss of a 14-point lead. Health and Rest Are Next The bye week offers a crucial chance for the roster to heal up before the final stretch of the season. Several key players, including running back Kyle Monangai and cornerback Tyrique Stevenson, have missed games this year and need this time to recover. Quarterback Caleb Williams also gets a week to rest his hamstring, while wide receiver Luther Burden III uses the time to recover from a concussion suffered in the game. Yahoo Sports reported that the power rankings have shifted dramatically at the midway point of the season, with only half of the preseason top 10 teams remaining in the top 10. The Bears have moved into a strong position, but the coach says the team still needs to improve its play to reach its full potential. Johnson said the team needs to continue evolving so they can win in the right manner, not just by luck or grit alone. The team will use this week to review the first nine games and decide what areas need the most work before the season ends.

item.title: Hawks Are Hot, But The Eastern Conference Reality Check Is Here
item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The Atlanta Hawks are sitting pretty at 7-5, but that record might be a bit of a mirage. Monday’s loss to the Los Angeles Lakers ended their four-game winning streak, placing them fourth in the Eastern Conference. The team has had a solid start, yet the gap between looking good and being a real contender is wide. Sports Illustrated notes that the Hawks have played more games than any other league team so far, indicating a brutal schedule. Staying in the upper echelon of the East currently requires winning against bad teams. With a combined 2-20 record, the Chicago Bulls and Milwaukee Bucks rank as two of the worst NBA teams. If the Hawks drop games against these bottom-tier squads, they will fall fast. To keep pace, Atlanta must take care of business against the worst of the bunch. Dyson Daniels Is The Only True Star While the offense can be shaky, Dyson Daniels is doing something special on both ends of the floor. Although Jalen Johnson receives more hype, he is arguably Atlanta’s most impactful player right now. Daniels just posted 10 points, eight rebounds, and six assists against the Lakers, along with four steals. For the whole season, he holds a team-best plus-58 rating when he is on the court. He is the Hawks’ best defender, and without him, the mediocre defense would be much worse. As the team prepares to face Chicago, he demonstrates high-level play as one of the NBA’s most underrated impact players. Julius Okongwu has posted 16 or more points in each of his last three outings and recorded nine rebounds in four of his last five contests. He has a plus-38 rating in his minutes. Lu Dort And The Backup Center Problem Not everyone is playing well, and Lu Dort is the biggest concern for the coaching staff. It has not been a great season for him in Atlanta, and the loss to the Lakers showed why. Dort scored only four points and shot 1-for-6 from three against the Lakers. He is a minus-38 in his minutes, the lowest on the entire team. When he does not shoot well, his defense is not good enough to justify the heavy minutes he is getting. The center position is another headache. Jock Landale returned from injury but played only 14 minutes against the Lakers and finished with five points. It was a questionable move to play him over rookie Zuby Ejiofor, who only played 3:52. Landale was not exceptional in his time, and the backup minutes remain a puzzle for Quin Snyder. According to reports, the Hawks rank 16th in points allowed per 100 possessions, marking them as a middle-of-the-pack defense. If they lose to Chicago or Milwaukee, it will be because they could not stop the other team’s offense. Friday night will see the Hawks resume play on the road against the Chicago Bulls.

item.title: Rangers Eye Sato But Phillies Could Land Power Hitter First
item.description: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images The Texas Rangers are showing interest in Japanese star Teruaki Sato, but a deal there looks like a long shot. According to Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon of The Athletic, the club is just one of several teams watching the market. The Phillies are also among the suitors, which puts Philadelphia in a prime spot to make a move if the price stays reasonable. This year’s free agent class likely features Sato as the premier position player, and his power bat might solve a lineup requiring more punch. Texas has bigger financial headaches than a new outfielder right now. The club is focused on shedding obligations to stars like Corey Seager, Jacob deGrom, and Nathan Eovaldi. MLB Trade Rumors predicted Sato would sign a five-year, $80 million deal, but other public estimates put the value well into the nine-figure range. The signing team also has to pay a posting fee based on that contract value. With the Rangers ending the 2026 season with a $218.7 million luxury tax number, spending big on Sato seems unlikely given their current payroll constraints. Power Comes With Strikeout Risks This year, Sato has hit 39 home runs for the Hashin Tigers, generating immense power from the left side. Across 614 plate appearances, he followed that performance with a .306/.383/.609 slash line. However, evaluators have questions about his pure hitting ability against better pitching. In a league where pitcher quality falls below Major League Baseball standards, he struck out at a 26.7 percent rate. Sato has a decent chance of punching out 30 percent of the time in the big leagues. Teams might accept those whiffs if he keeps hitting 30 or more homers, but it is a risky bet. Fit In Texas Or Philly While Sato has primarily played third base in Japan, numerous scouts believe he is better suited for a corner outfield role in the majors. Josh Jung secures the hot corner for Texas, but the team faces a vacancy at designated hitter as Joc Pederson explores free agency. They could also sign a left fielder while designating Wyatt Langford as the everyday center fielder. The Phillies need a left-handed bat to balance their lineup, and Sato fits that need perfectly. If the Rangers pull back due to cost, Philadelphia could swoop in to grab a player who hit 40 homers just one season ago. An estimated $192.8 million cash payroll and a $218.7 million luxury tax number marked the end of the 2026 season for the Rangers.

item.title: 49ers’ Fred Warner Sparks Blunt Words From Cowboys’ Dak Prescott
item.description: (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) Getty The San Francisco 49ers defense will be looking to make life challenging for the Dallas Cowboys‘ offense. San Francisco’s defense will be looking to carry over their defensive performance in Week 9 against the Las Vegas Raiders into this game. Against the Raiders, the Niners’ defense recorded five takeaways, including three interceptions and two forced fumbles. Fred Warner was one of the players who recorded a takeaway against the Silver and Black. Ahead of the game against the 49ers, Dallas Cowboys QB Dak Prescott shared his thoughts on facing Warner. Their offensive unit will have to account for where the linebacker is on the field and will need to hold on tight to the football, as Warner will be there to try to punch it out. “He’s probably the best linebacker in the NFL right now,” Prescott told reporters on Nov. 1 2. “The way he plays the game mentally, reading the splits, reading the back, whether he’s near or far, and making his different calls is impressive. “Their defense is simple because he can get them into the right positions. They play fast, and they play hard. There’s a little bit of a chess match there, but it’s no different from play callers calling the plays. At the end of the day, it’s about execution.” Warner has played 502 total snaps for the 49ers defense so far this season, leading to an 86.2 overall PFF defensive grade . Moreover, the veteran linebacker has recorded 54 solo tackles, generated five total pressures, one sack, 29 stops, and allowed an 84.6 passer rating when targeted in coverage. 49ers’ Fred Warner Draws More Praise From Cowboys Cowboys’ DeMarvion Overshown won’t be on the field at the same time as Warner, but the Dallas linebacker has a lot of respect for the 49ers star. “I have the utmost respect for him,” Overshown told reporters on Nov. 12 . “Since he came into this league, he’s been a dog. He’s been somebody you have to scout during the week. You have to know where 54 is and be aware when you’re carrying the ball. He’s the prototype linebacker. When you want to come into this league and be a great linebacker, you look at 54. “You look at Fred and what he’s done to change the game, especially how the linebacker position is played from sideline to sideline. I’d like to say he opened the doors for guys like me with my body type to come in and play four downs of football. I have the utmost respect for him. It’s going to be good watching him play, but it’s a battle at the end of the day. We want to come out as the linebacker unit that showed up and made the plays.” Fred Warner Gets Blunt on Facing Dallas’ Offense Meanwhile, Warner has plenty of respect for the Cowboys offense. Moreover, the veteran linebacker has recorded 54 solo tackles, generated five total pressures, one sack, 29 stops, and allowed an 84.6 passer rating when targeted in coverage. 49ers’ Fred Warner Draws More Praise From Cowboys Cowboys’ DeMarvion Overshown won’t be on the field at the same time as Warner, but the Dallas linebacker has a lot of respect for the 49ers star. “I have the utmost respect for him,” Overshown told reporters on Nov. 12 . “Since he came into this league, he’s been a dog. He’s been somebody you have to scout during the week. You have to know where 54 is and be aware when you’re carrying the ball. He’s the prototype linebacker. When you want to come into this league and be a great linebacker, you look at 54. “You look at Fred and what he’s done to change the game, especially how the linebacker position is played from sideline to sideline. I’d like to say he opened the doors for guys like me with my body type to come in and play four downs of football. I have the utmost respect for him. It’s going to be good watching him play, but it’s a battle at the end of the day. We want to come out as the linebacker unit that showed up and made the plays.” Fred Warner Gets Blunt on Facing Dallas’ Offense Meanwhile, Warner has plenty of respect for the Cowboys offense. On Nov. 11, the veteran linebacker spoke to the media and talked about Dallas’ offense, as they’ll be looking to make that unit’s life difficult in this contest. Warner noted that the 49ers need to be on their A-game, given that the Cowboys can hurt them in the passing game. “Dak [Prescott has] always played at a high level at the quarterback position,” Warner told reporters . “A guy I got a ton of respect for as a player and as a leader for their team. He has some really elite weapons on the outside. “CeeDee [Lamb] is having a tremendous year, getting a lot of targets, but also making use of those targets. George Pickens is also a huge weapon and has freakish ability when he gets the ball in his hands.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post 49ers’ Fred Warner Sparks Blunt Words From Cowboys’ Dak Prescott appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: SEC Football Week 11 Predictions: Picks for Every Game

You’re on your own if you want to risk it. However, several SEC teams will be in CFP mix even with a third loss, but the freakout will come if Alabama, Texas, Tennessee, and/or Kentucky get that third hit. Even worse, it’s over if any of the three-loss teams – South Carolina, LSU, Ole Miss, or Missouri – lose. Here are our quick previews and predictions for every SEC game. – Predictions: ACC | Big Ten SEC Week 11 Previews, Predictions Nov 7, 2026; Knoxville, Tennessee, USA; Kentucky Wildcats quarterback Kenny Minchey (3) calls a play at the line of scrimmage against the Tennessee Volunteers during the first quarter at Neyland Stadium. It’s a dangerous week for Alabama and Tennessee, going on the road to deal with desperate Mississippi State and Vanderbilt teams, respectively. The pressure will mostly be on Kentucky. It dropped big in the CFP after loss to Tennessee, and it can’t afford a loss to Florida. The Bulldog defense has been great, but the offense isn’t moving well enough to push past a decent D. Auburn might be working too hard, but the defensive front is great at getting into the backfield and should come up with just enough big stops late to hold off a late Bulldog rally in a terrific game. First, it has to take down a Vanderbilt team that finally came up with its first SEC win of the season, beating Mississippi State 25-23. Alabama might not be its sharpest out of the gate – a hangover effect from the 31-13 win at LSU – but just when it seems like this might be interesting, the Commodore turnovers will come. Bama will convert off all three turnovers it generates. Prediction: Alabama 37, Vanderbilt 17 Consensus Line: Alabama -18.5, o/u

The defense was brilliant in a 23-7 win over Florida, but it won’t have the same luck against an Ole Miss offense that needs to stop turning the ball over. Reynolds Razorback Stadium, Fayetteville, AR Don’t get totally caught up in the latest College Football Playoff rankings. Soon, there will be big arguments about several three-loss teams and how worthy they might be. South Carolina started 2-3, but it’s rolling with a four-game winning streak. That’s not why the CFP No. 17 team has reason to dream of finishing in the top 12. Next week? Georgia. Beat the No. 1 team, drop Clemson, and all of a sudden, there will be a discussion. First, it has to get by a plucky Arkansas team that’s far better than the 3-6 record might indicate. Nothing comes easy for the Gamecocks. Star quarterback LaNorris Sellers is banged up, but he’s expected to go. Fortunately for 16, Arkansas doesn’t have a pass rush to get to him. As long as Sellers is sniffing around a 65% completion rate, the Gamecocks will get through another grind of a game, and then it’s on to the Bulldogs. item.title: Bournemouth and Nottingham Forest battle Newcastle for highly-rated Santos starlet eyed by Bayern Munich
item.description: Santos v Palmeiras - Brasileirao 2026 - Getty Images Sport Bournemouth and Nottingham Forest are leading the Premier League chase to sign highly-rated Santos midfielder Gabriel Bontempo during the January transfer window. The English duo face stiff competition from Newcastle United for the 21-year-old Brazilian, who also attracted an enquiry from Bayern Munich over the summer. English clubs target Brazilian prospect According to TEAMtalk , the race for Bontempo is gathering pace as top-flight recruitment teams prepare mid-season approaches for one of South America's most sought-after emerging talents. Capable of operating effectively across several midfield and attacking roles, the versatile playmaker has developed rapidly at domestic level over recent months. His progress was recently rewarded with a senior international call-up to Carlo Ancelotti's latest Brazil squad . Scouting networks drive winter interest The report states that Forest's acclaimed South American scouting network is strongly pushing the City Ground hierarchy to explore a formal move for the youngster ahead of the New Year. Recruitment chiefs in the East Midlands have already built a strong reputation for identifying talent in the region after their groundwork helped bring Murillo, Jair Cunha and Igor Jesus to the club's attention. Meanwhile, the Cherries have emerged as serious contenders after lodging their own enquiries as they assess midfield options in case Alex Scott moves on. Having already demonstrated their willingness to recruit directly from the Brazilian market by signing Rayan last January, the south-coast outfit are keen to explore another deal in the country this winter. European heavyweights join growing queue Up on Tyneside, sporting director Ross Wilson and newly appointed head of recruitment Tomas Amaral are also monitoring the situation closely as they evaluate long-term additions. Both executives possess extensive knowledge of the South American market, while fellow English top-flight sides Brighton & Hove Albion and Brentford have also made initial enquiries as they track emerging prospects in Brazil. Beyond the Premier League, insiders note that clubs across Italy, Spain and Germany are keeping tabs on his trajectory after the Bavarian giants asked about his situation during the summer window. That widespread continental interest underlines the fierce competition for his signature and ensures the Vila Belmiro hierarchy will face mounting pressure over the coming months. Long contract strengthens negotiating stance Despite the growing clamour from overseas suitors, Santos hold a commanding position ahead of the January market as Bontempo remains tied to the club until 2030. The Brazilian side have no intention of allowing one of their brightest stars to depart on the cheap and will demand a substantial financial package before considering any approach. Consequently, Forest, Bournemouth and their European rivals face tough negotiations to secure a winter t

item.title: Ireland bounce back to beat UAE in Emerging Nations
item.description: Ireland secured a comfortable 61-run victory [Getty Images] Second T20 international, Ajman Ireland Women 171-5 (20 overs): Lewis 71, Maritz 29; Thirukkumaran 2-20 United Arab Emirates Women 110-8 (20 overs): Oza 51, Dharnidharka 18; Murray 2-21 Ireland Women win by 61 runs Scorecard Ireland Women recovered from their opening Emerging Nations Trophy defeat by Sri Lanka to claim a comfortable 61-run victory against United Arab Emirates in their second game in Ajman. The UAE won the toss and elected to field first, with Lloyd Tennant's side producing a much stronger showing with the bat than they did against Sri Lanka. The opening partnership of vice-captain Amy Hunter and captain Gaby Lewis laid the foundations for the Irish. Hunter managed 29 runs from 27 balls before she was run out by Suraksha Kotte, while Lewis finished as Ireland's top run scorer with 71, including 12 fours and a six before she was dismissed by Indhuja Nandakumar in the 12th over. Janani Thirukkumaran then forced out Louise Little (seven) in the next over and claimed her second wicket from Lara Maritz soon after, although she did add 29 to Ireland's tally from just 23 balls. Laura Delany was 18 not out while Theertha Satish ran out Alana Dazell (11) as Ireland finished on 171-5 from their 20 overs. The UAE had a nightmare start to their response as they lost Satish, Heena Hotchandhani and Rinitha Rajith all inside the first two overs. Samaira Dharnidharka added 18 to the tally before becoming the fourth player to exit when she was bowled out by Cara Murray in the seventh over. Esha Oza steadied the ship as she registered 51 runs from 45 balls with five fours and a six before being dismissed by Little. The wickets continued to tumble as Thirukkumaran (13), Mehul Kulkarni (six) and Athige Sashikala Silva (four) all went as UAE fell well short of the target, ending with 110-8. Ireland will next be in action on Monday when they face face Papua New Guinea (09:15 GMT) before rounding off their group campaign with a game against Scotland on Wednesday, 18 November (05:00 GMT).

item.title: ‘This break came at the ideal moment for me’: Senne Lammens happy to escape Manchester United crisis for a week of international football
item.description: ‘This break came at the ideal moment for me’: Senne Lammens happy to escape Manchester United crisis for a week of international football It is fair to say that Senne Lammens has not been enjoying the best of times at Manchester United in the past few weeks. However, on Thursday evening Lammens was able to escape the crisis that has been engulfing Manchester United in recent weeks and join up with the Belgian national team . Despite his dip in form at club level, Mark van Bommel stuck with Lammens in goal against Türkiye as Belgium won 2-1 away from home. Speaking to the media after the game, Lammens reflected on what has been a tough time in Manchester. The goalkeeper said ‘ This break came at the ideal moment for me ‘. There had been some rumours that perhaps van Bommel would opt for a different goalkeeper, with Mike Penders having done well for Chelsea in recent weeks. However, the former Antwerp head coach stuck with Lammens and the Manchester United goalkeeper made a number of saves to ensure Belgium took all three points. Lammens felt good after the game, before also saying ‘ These have been difficult weeks for me at Manchester United ‘. On his return to his club after the break, Lammens will be operating under a new head coach. With Michael Carrick gone, the 24-year-old will be looking to impress the new head coach, which looks to be Mauricio Pochettino. Lammens did speak about Carrick’s departure, saying ‘ The team really did support the manager, but when the results don’t follow, you know this can happen. We know that we have to do much better ‘. GBeNeFN | Ben Jackson

item.title: England thrashed by Australia in first ODI to provide welcome distraction to sandpaper scandal
item.description: England crashed to a heavy defeat in the first game of their latest Australian tour, with a rousing debut from 21-year-old Mahli Beardman diverting some of the home side’s attention from the ongoing sandpaper scandal . Australian cricket is in the midst of a bitter civil war over Usman Khawaja’s historic ball-tampering allegations but the hosts still eased to a seven-wicket victory in in the first ODI in Perth , where local boy Beardman collected stunning figures of six for 24. It proved another calamitous visit to Optus Stadium for England, who thew away the first Ashes Test in two days on the same ground 12 months ago. With Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood all rested between Test series, Australia pieced together an inexperienced attack and watched as it dismantled their rivals. At one stage England were 65 for eight and staring at a record low total, with some late repair work by the tail lifting them to 131 all out. Travis Head missed the chance to repeat his match-winning Ashes knock when he was bowled cheaply by Gus Atkinson but skipper Mitch Marsh took up the mantle, clubbing 50 off just 30 balls to lead a chase that was all over in less than 24 overs. England were criticised last winter for being too casual in their preparations Down Under but that has not been the case this time. They have trained hard, given themselves time to acclimatise and beaten Western Australia in a warm-up game at the WACA. All of that work came to nothing, though, as they followed up a disappointing tri-series in Pakistan with a fourth loss in their last five outings. After being sent in England’s openers scraped together 24 before Australia bagged their first, Ben Duckett slashing Spencer Johnson to backward point. Ben Duckett was the first English batsman to get out (AP) Tom Banton came closer than anyone to finding form, hitting five fours on his way to 25 before driving with hard hands at the tidy Xavier Bartlett. An average start then transformed into a dreadful once as the introduction of Beardman plunged the innings into turmoil. Kicking off his senior international career with England’s two best batters at the crease, the youngster got the best of both. His eighth ball was sharp and well directed, with enough swing to take the outside edge as Harry Brook went back in defence. Joe Root , on the day he became just the third Englishman to 200 ODI appearances, was even bigger scalp. Muddling his way to 17 from 36 balls, he was put down by Cooper Connolly on three before an optimistic drive off Beardman wound up in Josh Inglis’ gloves. The celebrations showed how much that wicket meant but he was just warming up. Jordan Cox followed to another defensive nick and Beardman showed his range by bouncing out Sam Curran , who hooked obligingly to fine leg for a seven-ball duck. Liam Dawson also fell without score, the fifth victim of a dream debut. Australia made easy work of their 131 chase (AP) England’s woes continued as Jamie Overton ’s ugly top-edge

Liam Dawson also fell without score, the fifth victim of a dream debut. Australia made easy work of their 131 chase (AP) England’s woes continued as Jamie Overton ’s ugly top-edge was plucked one-handed by the returning Johnson but Will Jacks ’ 25 and Atkinson’s punchy 29 not out saw them double their total. Beardman returned to end the innings, dismissing Jofra Archer to claim record debut figures for Australia and match England’s best ever analysis in the format, by Reece Topley in 2022. Atkinson bowled Head with his first delivery but Australia never threatened to let the result slip. Marsh put his foot down, blazing four sixes and four fours, effectively settling the matter by the time flicked Overton to deep-midwicket in the ninth over. Banton misjudged a steepling catch to spare Connolly on five, who added 22 more before poking Archer to gully. Inglis and Matt Renshaw did the rest with minimal fuss, leaving 159 deliveries unused.

item.title: Harry Kane breaks England appearance record and moves sixth for all-time international goals
item.description: Harry Kane breaks England appearance record and moves sixth for all-time international goals Harry Kane is now England 's most-capped men's player of all time after winning his 126th cap in a 2-1 Nations League victory over Croatia at Wembley. The England captain moves clear of goalkeeper Peter Shilton, whose 125 caps were won between 1970 and 1990. Kane had drawn level with Shilton last month, scoring twice as England beat the Czech Republic 3-0 at Wembley. The 33-year-old's record night arrives less than three weeks after he became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or. Ahead of the game, he spoke about his favourite England memories and named his 'biggest dream' as he chases major team trophies. A Wembley send-off fit for a record breaker Wembley marked the milestone before kick-off. A giant tifo of Kane was unfurled in the west stand, and the striker showed his Ballon d'Or trophy to the crowd. Shilton handed over a commemorative cap, Prince William presented a framed shirt and Croatia captain Luka Modric gave Kane a glass-encased football. It was a replica of the first ball the English took to Croatia in 1880. Kane also had a hand in the opening goal. Playing deeper in midfield, he slipped a diagonal pass through for Jude Bellingham down the right, and Bellingham cut it back for Morgan Rogers to score. The appearance record sits alongside the goalscoring one. Kane passed the old England mark of 53 goals in March 2023, and the Bayern Munich forward now has 92 international goals. He's now equal sixth for international goals in men's football , level with Robert Lewandowski. Romelu Lukaku (94) is the only active player ahead of Kane on the all-time list, after Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi's recent retirements. England play Spain in Madrid on Sunday, and a win would make Thomas Tuchel's side seeded for the Nations League quarter-finals at Easter, with the finals to follow next June.

item.title: Bears Stadium Bids Flood In As Developers Push City Plan
item.description: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images Developers are flooding the market with unsolicited bids to keep the Chicago Bears in the city, but the team’s focus remains on a suburban deal or a move to Indiana. This bid arrives as the Bears prepare for a legislative session in Illinois starting Nov. 17, yet the franchise has not endorsed any of these urban proposals. The group plans to span about 100 acres and include a stadium for 75,000 fans alongside thousands of new homes. They argue that an urban site offers better economic value than remote suburbs. “It is our belief that a modern, competitive dome stadium such as the one that we are proposing will outperform suburban locations such as Arlington Heights or northwest Indiana,” said Quintin Primo III, founder and executive chairman of Capri Investment Group, during a news conference in Bronzeville, according to Yahoo . Local leaders back the idea, but the NFL has previously flagged the specific Reese parcel as too narrow with active rail lines running through it. City Dreams Versus Team Reality While local boosters push for a downtown solution, the Bears are actively exploring a path across the state line. Nearly nine months ago, Indiana state leaders approved a funding package, and due diligence has been completed regarding two potential locations in Hammond. The team has not commented on the specific Chicago proposals but is watching the Illinois political process closely. “We expect productive dialogue with both leadership teams in the coming weeks,” the Bears said last week regarding the two states, according to Yahoo Sports . The franchise is seeking property tax certainty and infrastructure help, with its main focus still on its own land in suburban Arlington Heights. Capri’s group is prepared to purchase the Bears’ current Arlington Heights property, which would solve the land issue but force the team to abandon its preferred suburban setup. Chicago 4th Ward Alderman Lamont Robinson voiced strong support for the Bronzeville plan, stating it serves the community best. “I believe with everything I have, it’s the right thing for the 4th ward. And the right thing for Chicago and the bears,” Robinson said. The developers claim their plan will shape the city for generations, but the team holds the real power in the negotiation. The Clock Ticks on Illinois Newly reelected Gov. JB Pritzker intends to advance a Bears-related bill during the upcoming veto session, creating a critical moment for the stadium saga. The recent rise in developer activity suggests growing confidence that a bill could pass, even as the team keeps its Indiana option alive. The Reese option joins similar unsolicited offers made in recent weeks for sites at the former South Works steel mill and Rate Field. “We have an opportunity to make a decision that will shape Chicago for generations,” said Quintin Primo III, Capri founder and executive chairman. The Bears must decide soon if they will stay in the city or leave for a new home. Due dili

item.title: Bloomington South girls basketball win over North completes county sweep
item.description: Just two weeks into the season and the Bloomington South girls basketball team has vanquished it's two county rivals. The annual meeting with Bloomington North was pushed up a month earlier than in the past, with the Cougars needing to adjust their schedule as new members of the Mid-State Conference. So it was a great early-season introduction to a sectional-like atmosphere for both teams in front of a vocal crowd at South on Thursday, Nov. 12. Offense was hard to come by as the Panthers held off a second-half rally by North, getting a huge 3-pointer from freshman Quinn Wurtzman with 2:10 left in a five-point game to pull out a 48-37 win. It followed a much less rowdy 62-20 rout of Edgewood on Tuesday. More: Senior seldomly comes off field for Bloomington South football "We knew it was going to be a great crowd," North coach Kiley Jarrett said. "That's what we wanted. We wanted to simulate a playoff atmosphere and that's what it was. "I just think we just got in too big of a hole in the first half. We fought like hell to get it back within five points and a just a couple possessions here and there that made the difference." Emotions were also running high with South junior transfer Kate Lehr playing her first game against her old mates. She came out fiery to score eight of her 12 points in the first period. From there, the offense spread out among the top eight, with six scoring with five points or more. "Playing them this early, I kind of figured it would be like that," South coach Larry Winters said. "I say it often, if they'd play with the same energy against us against other teams, they'd come out with the win. They came out, 1, because Kate's here but 2, because they always play us that way. "And tonight they did a really good job because they kept our two scorers from scoring." South finished 15-of-48 shooting, hitting 5 of 16 3-pointers but also going 13-of-15 at the line. "We were trying to score more than in any other game," Winters said. "We talked about that, let the shots find you, don't try to find the shots. Tonight, we tried to find the shots. But everybody wants to show out in front of every one, so that's what happens." Winters is confident the offense will get back on track since so many have been contributing so far. "They can all score and if you're sharing the ball, that's going to happen," Winters said. "Annika (Smith) was 1-for-10 and Tatum (DeVries) took three shots. There's going to be nights like that gives an opportunity for somebody else to step up and do something. "If teams want to concentrate on a couple players when you have as many as we do, then somebody just has to step up." We wanted to simulate a playoff atmosphere and that's what it was. "I just think we just got in too big of a hole in the first half. We fought like hell to get it back within five points and a just a couple possessions here and there that made the difference." Emotions were also running high with South junior transfer Kate Lehr playing her first game against her old mates. She came out fiery to score eight of her 12 points in the first period. From there, the offense spread out among the top eight, with six scoring with five points or more. "Playing them this early, I kind of figured it would be like that," South coach Larry Winters said. "I say it often, if they'd play with the same energy against us against other teams, they'd come out with the win. They came out, 1, because Kate's here but 2, because they always play us that way. "And tonight they did a really good job because they kept our two scorers from scoring." South finished 15-of-48 shooting, hitting 5 of 16 3-pointers but also going 13-of-15 at the line. "We were trying to score more than in any other game," Winters said. "We talked about that, let the shots find you, don't try to find the shots. Tonight, we tried to find the shots. But everybody wants to show out in front of every one, so that's what happens." Winters is confident the offense will get back on track since so many have been contributing so far. "They can all score and if you're sharing the ball, that's going to happen," Winters said. "Annika (Smith) was 1-for-10 and Tatum (DeVries) took three shots. There's going to be nights like that gives an opportunity for somebody else to step up and do something. "If teams want to concentrate on a couple players when you have as many as we do, then somebody just has to step up." North digs hole in first half South (2-1) will always lean on its defense, and forcing 11 turnovers in the first half led to some easy buckets and a 29-16 lead at the break. North had some key players in early foul trouble and the physical affects of the South press led to some 'tired' errors. "It was just mistakes on our part," Jarrett said. "Foul trouble didn't help us at all, it got us out of our typical rotation." But the Panthers' offensive struggles peaked in the third, going 2-of-11, forcing up some tough shots in the lane all night. That allowed the Cougars (0-2), who had just five more turnovers and played strong half-court defense most of the night, to chip away at the deficit. "We know that when we play them that if we can keep them in the half-court and not turn the ball over, then we're going to be in good shape," Jarrett said. North got within 33-27 at the end of three, but South wouldn't let them get any closer. A jump hook by Quinnly Fife and a banked in 3 by Avery Schwartzman from the top of the key while being fouled made it 38-29 with 6:26 to go. But a 3 from Rilynn Williams, who had a game high 13 points, made it 40-35 with 2:40 left. "She definitely is a more assertive player this year," Jarrett said. "And she stepped up tonight and made some huge plays for us. That 3 from the corner was absolutely huge. And I thought she did a good job defensively on Lehr." But that's when Wurtzman took the next big shot of the night, knocking home a 3 from 22 feet to start an 8-0 run that put the game away. "Knowing Quinn, she was ready for that shot and she'll be ready for that again," Jarrett said "It may say she's a freshman but she doesn't play like it and we knew that coming in. "Credit to her. That was a momentum changer because I definitely felt like momentum was on our side before that." All the same, Winters is looking at the big picture with his younger players. "That was a big 3 but there were three layups she missed," Winters said. "If you're going to make the long one, make the short one. But that's the pressure of playing in your first North-South game." More: 20 Bloomington area girls basketball returning players to watch in 2026-27 season Growing pains for Edgewood South started the week with a 62-20 win at Edgewood, a game that got away quickly after the young Mustangs tied it at 8-8 with 1:40 left in the first quarter. The Panthers scored the next 22 points as Edgewood coughed it up 20 times in the first half. It was 31-10 at the break and South put the running clock in motion late in the third, up 49-13. Edgewood was limited to four field goals, just one inside the arc. The frustration was evident, but South is also likely the best team the Mustangs will see all season. "You just have to harp on the positive things that we did," Edgewood coach Noah Stuckey said. "I feel like, that first quarter, we competed as well as we possibly could. We handled their physicality and got to the free throw line and then we just kinds of wore down. "We got punched and wilted a little bit and didn't bring the energy in the second half." It was just the second varsity team for the entire lineup so the speed and strength it takes to succeed at that level was on display. On either side of that loss against the best team on their schedule, the Mustangs opened with a win over Greencastle 42-32 and then topped South Putnam 40-31 on Thursday. "It felt awkward," Stuckey said of the win over Greencastle. "We started very strong, we got in some foul trouble and they made a run at us. Then, the second half, Kaitlyn (Ripley) took over. She didn't play the second quarter and had 23 points. "The way they've been playing maybe the last couple of years is just stand and watch her," Stuckey said. "And we just can't rely on her to do everything. We've got to help her out and we kind of got in that run in the second and third quarter (against South)." item.title: Coldwater's Delaney leads 2026 Battle Creek Enquirer All-Enquirer Boys Soccer Team
item.description: BATTLE CREEK - Never losing a game from late August until October. Winning a conference title and a district crown. For helping his team accomplish all of that, Coldwater's Ken Delaney is the 2026 All-Enquirer Boys Soccer Team Coach of the Year. The All-Enquirer Boys Soccer Team is selected by nominations from the city and area coaches and voted on by the Enquirer sports staff. MORE: Player capsules for the Battle Creek Enquirer All-Enquirer Boys Soccer Team In his 18th season as head coach, Delaney is on a roll with state-ranked teams in back-to-back years as the Cardinals were 15-2-2 overall. Coldwater finished as Interstate 8 Conference champs with a 6-0 record in the league and won a second district title in the last three years. Along the way, Coldwater went unbeaten from August 20 until the regionals and climbed to as high as No. 12 in the Michigan Interscholastic High School Soccer Coaches rankings in Division 2. Delaney is joined on the All-Enquirer team by Cardinals players Abdulhamid Munassar, Ahmen Norman, Riath Shamaala and Jensely Norvilus. Lakeview finished as All-City Tournament champs and adds Mang Sung, Richard Lian and Cristian Duran to the team. Harper Creek had the most wins in program history as Beavers' Jake Cushman, Broderick Hanger and TJ Ruble were named All-Enquirer. Also from the city, earning All-Enquirer honors, are Pennfield's Philipp Kruetz and Everett Wilkins, Battle Creek Central's Yoani Bautista Trejo and Deangelo Crape, with the St. Philip/Calhoun co-op program adding Ashton Heighton and Ben Kaczanowski. Among area teams, Marshall's Brandon Baker, Rowdy Joseph, Carson Clapper and Trenton Wolkiewicz were named as All-Enquirer members, as well as Gull Lake's Charlie Trantham, Ethan Waldorf. Bill Broderick can be reached at bbroderi@battlecreekenquirer.com. Follow him on X /Twitter: @billbroderick This article originally appeared on Battle Creek Enquirer: Coldwater's Delaney leads 2026 Battle Creek Enquirer All-Enquirer Boys Soccer Team

item.title: Legendary coach Terry Waters finds new role at Fishburne
item.description: WAYNESBORO — Terry Waters is a legendary wrestling coach in the area. He was inducted into the Virginia Chapter of the National Wrestling Hall of Fame in 2022, and his photo and biographical info are in the National Wrestling Hall of Fame in Stillwater, Oklahoma. Most assumed he would coach wrestling until he retired and then just walk away. Raised in a hot bed of wrestling in Pennsylvania, Waters was a student at Milton Hershey School, a boarding school for low-income families in Hershey. He and his brother were among the first Black students at the school after it integrated. Locally, Waters has coached at Staunton, Riverheads and Fort Defiance high schools, as well as at Washington & Lee University, where he was an assistant. He came to Fishburne in 2015. This past summer, he announced he was retiring from coaching. It seemed to be the end of an amazing career, but then he announced, not too longer afterward, that he would be staying at the Waynesboro school to serve as athletic director. He's now through the fall season and about to start winter sports. "It hasn't gone totally smooth, but it's been a great transition," Waters said. "The thing is I still get to coordinate a lot with the kids. That was the big decision for me, how much involvement would I get to have with the kids." He is now dealing with 20 or so coaches, not just his own assistants like he did as wrestling coach. That has been challenging. "You're dealing with 20, 24 personalities," he said. "That becomes a situation where you have to take a step back and try to understand each coach individually." Coaching for 49 years, Waters feels he had a great relationship with most of his athletic directors. He has tried to take lessons he learned from them into this job. He learned what kind of athletic director he wanted to be and what kind he didn't want to be. "I wanted to be fair, and I believe that I'm open and positive if a coach wants to talk with me," he said. "Obviously taking over a new position, you want to change some things — your approach and things like that — but overall it's gone pretty well." Fishburne offers 10 sports. Asked if he ever thought about being an athletic director, Waters took a long pause before answering. He said maybe it was in the back of his mind, but it was never something he really pursued. "When this happened, I really think it was God opening the door," Waters said. "This situation just came open." "The thing is I still get to coordinate a lot with the kids. That was the big decision for me, how much involvement would I get to have with the kids." He is now dealing with 20 or so coaches, not just his own assistants like he did as wrestling coach. That has been challenging. "You're dealing with 20, 24 personalities," he said. "That becomes a situation where you have to take a step back and try to understand each coach individually." Coaching for 49 years, Waters feels he had a great relationship with most of his athletic directors. He has tried to take lessons he learned from them into this job. He learned what kind of athletic director he wanted to be and what kind he didn't want to be. "I wanted to be fair, and I believe that I'm open and positive if a coach wants to talk with me," he said. "Obviously taking over a new position, you want to change some things — your approach and things like that — but overall it's gone pretty well." Fishburne offers 10 sports. Asked if he ever thought about being an athletic director, Waters took a long pause before answering. He said maybe it was in the back of his mind, but it was never something he really pursued. "When this happened, I really think it was God opening the door," Waters said. "This situation just came open." Every year, at least in recent years, someone would ask the veteran coach how much longer. His answer was always one more year. He'd talk with his wife about his future in coaching after the season ended. She would tell him if he still had the energy and the desire, he should keep coaching. "My brother pretty much summed it up when he told me if you like what you're doing, there is no sense in retiring," he said. But this summer, he clearly remembers waking up one morning and thinking, "I'm done." He told the Fishburne staff about his decision. He was planning to just walk away, but then the athletic director position opened. Waters decided to apply. "I've had athletic directors across the state send me notes telling me if I needed any help just let them know," Waters said. He said Frank Kahrs at Grace Christian has been particularly helpful. He's also talked with Staunton's David Tibbs about some questions he had. All the connections Waters has built over the years are proving to be helpful in the new job. "I believe I'm here because it's where God wants me," Waters said. The day-to-day life of an athletics director is never the same, and never boring, Waters said. "You spend a lot more time than I actually though on the computer," he said, "sending emails out, setting schedules, things like that." It's about a 10-hour a day job, give or take, and Waters said he's fine with that. He does have two assistant athletic directors that help take some of the burden off of him, but Waters said he'll be at every home event at Fishburne. He feels it's his responsibility. "I love what I do," he said. Wrestling this winter may be the toughest for him because he's not coaching — although, maybe not. "I don't think I'm going to miss it as much as other people think I'm going to miss it," Waters said. "I just want to make sure I don't step on toes." Rick Palmer is taking over as head wrestling coach at Fishburne. Waters said he has confidence in Palmer's abilities to continue leading the program. Still, Waters said home wrestling events will be difficult, sitting in the stands watching instead of in the corner of the mat coaching. "That is something that will be hard," he said, "but I'm prepared for that. I've done all I want to do in coaching in 49 years. I don't have anything else to prove. I was ready to step down. I was comfortable in my decision." More: 'Last ride' for Wilson Memorial star Bree Kindig More: Tyree Scott takes Rollos BBQ from food truck to Craigsville shop Patrick Hite is a reporter at The News Leader.
